title: An agent can write .veil.toml with policy=log and turn every deny into allow
description: Reported by MagentaBass on bd-3qw (2026-11-26), measured at e3d9eff with the real binary in a throwaway HOME: veil makes no decision on a Write of .veil.toml; with [policy] default="log" in that file, a Read of a protected file is then allowed. Predates bd-3qw. Not re-run by the orchestrator. Needs a design call: how project config may weaken policy, and whether tool writes to it are refused.
close_reason: Verified at 982ad2c (code = 22755f1; CI 45829576726 green, 5 jobs). Orchestrator: new tests on bdc5d6f fail 6 of 9 (project_floor) and 8 of 9 (config_guard); full suite 934 passed 0 failed; own real-binary probes: loosening project file still denies protected Read, cat, unresolved arg and MCP read; 10 config write targets incl. case variants and 23 shell write forms denied; ordinary write, cat of .veil.toml and git status not blocked. Operator confirmed the floor covers every project setting. KNOWN LIMIT: an unseen write that deletes or rewrites .veil.toml removes protections declared only there. Guard does not cover script files, archive extraction, tree copies, git checkout . / switch / pull / clean, rm -r of a parent, xargs stdin names, MCP write tools (builder's list, not re-tested). NO-CLAIM: orchestrator did not review every changed source line.

comments.author: zacharyruiz
comments.text:
DECISION NEEDED

Question: how should veil stop an agent from weakening its own project policy?

Today: an agent can write .veil.toml with [policy] default="log", after which a protected file can be read. Reported by a builder, measured at e3d9eff in a throwaway HOME; the orchestrator did not re-run it.

A (recommended): refuse agent writes to .veil.toml; people edit it themselves. Smallest change, but it only covers writes veil sees (see bd-ao5 and bd-u4u for commands it does not read).
B: a project's .veil.toml may only make policy stricter. Weakening it needs a setting outside the project that agents cannot write. Stronger, because it does not rely on seeing the write, but projects that use policy="log" would need to change.
C: both A and B.
D: accept the risk and document it.

To answer, comment on this bead starting with "DECISION:".

comments.author: zacruiz
comments.text: DECISION: C (both A and B). Refuse agent writes to .veil.toml AND enforce a monotonic policy floor so a repo-local .veil.toml may only tighten policy and cannot weaken default/global deny to log (weakening requires an explicit user-owned setting outside the project directory that agents cannot write). This closes both unhooked shell writes (bd-ao5/bd-u4u) and writable project trees under veil sandbox.

comments.author: zacharyruiz
comments.text: Operator confirmed (2026-11-26, in session: 'agree', replying to this reading): 'may only tighten' applies to every project .veil.toml setting, not only policy=log; for example a project cannot add approved tools or safe-file patterns, which go in the user config. Known limit also stated to the operator: the floor cannot stop an unseen write that removes protections declared only in .veil.toml.

title: Decide: is 10 minutes the right time limit for veil exec tools?
description:
DECISION NEEDED

Question: should the tool time limit stay at a fixed 10 minutes?

Today (added by the bd-oml fix, a builder's choice): a tool run through veil exec is stopped after 10 minutes (broker_tool_timed_out), also outside a sandbox. It cannot be configured. Processes the tool started are not stopped. The broker serves one call at a time, so a longer limit means other calls can wait longer.

A (recommended unless one of your tools can run longer): keep 10 minutes.
B: choose a different fixed limit (say how long).
C: make it configurable, in a setting an agent cannot write (see bd-02q).

To answer, comment on this bead starting with DECISION:
close_reason: Operator DECISION A (2026-11-26): keep the fixed 10 minute limit. No code change.

comments.author: zacruiz
comments.text: DECISION: A. Keep the fixed 10-minute tool time limit for veil exec for now; revisit configurability only if a real workload legitimately exceeds 10 minutes.

title: Hook refused a compound command that runs claude, saying claude is given claude as its program
description: Seen 2026-11-26 with the build of 982ad2c installed. The refused Bash command had this shape: assign a directory to a variable; mkdir -p it; cd into it; run claude -p with a long single-quoted prompt and a few options, piped to jq; then an if on whether a marker file exists. Reason given: claude is given claude as its program, which veil cannot resolve to a path (dynamic path, label protected). The simple command claude -p hello gets no decision. Which part triggers the refusal has not been isolated. First step: reduce it to a minimal real-binary test.

title: Track A: interpreter script-file inspection
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic. Depends on shell decomposition.

PROBLEM: 'python3 read.py' is ALLOWED while 'python3 -c ...' is denied. An agent can write a 3-line script and run it. Same for node x.js, ruby, perl, Rscript, deno, bun, bash script.sh.

DESIGN: When the simple command is an interpreter (python/python3/node/ruby/perl/Rscript/bun/deno/bash/sh/zsh) with a script path argument that exists and is < 256 KiB, read the script text (veil itself reading a script the agent wrote is not a boundary violation: the script is not protected data) and run the SAME accessor extraction used today for -c strings (open(), Path().read_text, pandas/polars read_*, fs.readFileSync, File.read, readLines, csv.reader, sqlite3.connect, duckdb) plus any literal path token that resolves into a protected directory. Deny if any resolves protected. Script larger than the cap -> deny with 'script_too_large_to_inspect' when a protected dir is in scope, else allow with audit.

NOTE: this is best-effort; the sandbox track is what makes it airtight. Say so in the remediation text.

TESTS: fixtures for python/node/ruby scripts reading a protected path directly, via variable, via os.path.join; negative fixture (script reads only a *-report.json).
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator at 0175c50: full suite on clean git-archive export 650 passed, 0 failed; CI green on 0175c50 and 30cbb2e. Interpreter script-file inspection (6ddaa25) plus fail-closed on opaque script tails (659b513); author recorded seven mutation checks (not re-run by me). Best effort by design (bounded scan); README states limits. Not verified: independent re-run of mutations; real interpreters beyond the tests.

comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
bd-1bk evidence (BrownChapel), commit 6ddaa25 on main. Not closed; closure needs an independent verifier.

WHAT SHIPPED
`python3 read.py` and its kin now read the script file and judge what is in it, like the same code given to `-c`. Script operand found for python/node/nodejs/bun/deno/ruby/perl/Rscript/bash/sh/zsh (versioned names too), `source`/`.`, files run by name with an interpreter first line (`./tools/read.py`), files a uv/poetry/pdm/deno wrapper runs (by extension), a Python directory (`__main__.py`) and a script on stdin from a file (`python3 < read.py`).
- Non-shell: the existing accessor extraction (open, Path.read_text, fs.readFileSync, File.read, readLines, ...) as for -c, plus every path-shaped quoted word, plus paths built from literals (os.path.join, Path `/`, `+`, f-strings, `${}`, `#{}`, File.join, path.join, file.path; constants assigned once).
- Shell scripts: text re-fed to the Bash decomposer, each command judged, scripts they run read in turn (depth 3).
- Limits: 256 KiB per script, 16 scripts, 1 MiB, 3 levels per Bash call; work per token bounded; only the first 512 words are checked against the filesystem (the rest lexically).
- Over a limit: judged like a recursive copy of the directory it runs in. Protected path in reach -> deny, reason_class `script_too_large_to_inspect`; none in reach -> allow, audit record says it was not read. Matches the bead's design.
- A script that is itself under a protected path: denied for being named; not read (contents never reach a reason).
- Denials name the script ("found in script `x`"), remediation says best effort and only an OS sandbox is airtight (bead NOTE). Audit origin `script`. `veil audit --class script_too_large_to_inspect` lists them (cli value_parser, operator.json, README updated).
- README: new "Script Files" section with what is read and what is not.

EVIDENCE (clean copy: HEAD bfc7d6a + exactly the 8 files committed, plus .beads swept in by the commit hook)
- `cargo test --locked`: 619 passed, 0 failed (351 lib incl. 25 in extract::script, 79 bin, 19 in tests/script_files.rs, rest the existing suites).
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- CI run 45686980063 on 6ddaa25: success (fmt, clippy, tests, ast-grep spine rules, doctor smoke).
- tests/script_files.rs drives the real veil binary with Claude Code Bash payloads against real script files. Covers the bead's TESTS list: python/node/ruby (and perl, R, deno, bun) reading a protected path directly, via variable, via os.path.join (2-part, 3-part, constant, Path `/`, f-string, `+`, chained constants, script-dir relative); negative fixture reading only q3-report.json/notes.md plus a plain script with decoy words -> allowed. Also: options/wrappers, stdin, shebang, python package dir, shell, `source`, 3-level chain allowed to read, 4-level chain -> script_too_large_to_inspect, protected script, 256 KiB boundary (at limit read, +1 refused), oversize deny vs allow+record, `veil audit --class`, padded 5000-decoy script still denied in bounded time, warn policy, comment FP pinned, no-script commands unchanged.
- Mutation checks, each applied to a scratch copy, each failed a test, then restored: (1) no script ever inspected: 16 integration + 2 unit fail; (2) protected-script skip removed: 1; (3) unread script always allowed: 3; (4) depth limit 3->30: 1; (5) filesystem budget removed: 1, UNIT TEST ONLY; (6) wrapper-extension detection off: 3; (7) stdin redirect ignored: 1.
- An adversarial-input unit test (`join(` x20000, 40000 commas, 40000 `[`) reads in under a second; before the MAX_SKIP/MAX_NESTING bounds the nested case was quadratic.

NAMED GAPS / HONEST LIMITS
1. Not independently verified. Re-execution only in this session; no second reader.
2. FALSE POSITIVES: (a) a path named in a comment or docstring is denied like code (pinned by a test, documented); (b) a script over 256 KiB (a minified Node bundle, say) that runs from a directory with a protected path in reach is denied, and there is no config knob for the cap. This is the bead's stated design but it will bite real repos; asking for a decision below.
3. NOT SEEN (documented in README): paths built at run time (env, files, input, network, imports; imports are not followed); scripts arriving via a pipe (`cat x.py | python3`); `python3 -m module`; zip/pyc/binary entrypoints; a script written earlier on the same line (does not exist yet); TOCTOU between hook and run; directory entry points other than Python `__main__.py`; shell-script words that expand (`"$1"`, `"$SRC"`) are not judged.
4. The 512-word filesystem budget is pinned only by a unit test (mutation 5). The integration padding test passes without it: it proves a path after 5000 decoys is still found in bounded time, not that the budget exists.
5. Scope beyond the bead's text: shebang files, stdin redirect, shell-script recursion, wrapper-extension detection, R accessors, constant folding of built paths, and the unread/limit machinery above. Added because each is a one-line bypass of the bead's own premise (`./read.py`, `uv run read.py`, `bash x.sh`), but it is more surface than the bead asked for and more for a verifier to read (src/extract/script.rs is ~1,900 lines including tests).
6. Priority: the bead is P1 here; the orchestrator's earlier ruling was P0/P1 only, so no conflict, but I had it as P2 in my notes.
7. `ubs` on the changed files reports criticals that are heuristic false positives (enum `kind == InterpreterKind::X` flagged as "secret compared with ==", `Instant::now` near `token` names flagged as weak randomness; same family as the known evaluator.rs/lib.rs hits). One real hit, a `panic!` in a unit test arm, was replaced with an assert after the scan; I did not re-run ubs after that edit.
8. macOS only (bash 3.2, Darwin). Nothing here ran on Linux except CI's.
9. Interpreter-run commands outside the list (`docker exec python x.py`, `ssh host python x.py`) are still not followed, as before.

DECISION NEEDED (orchestrator): should the 256 KiB cap get a `[policy]` knob, or an allowlist for known-big scripts? Default now: none (bead design). I did not add one.

NEXT: bd-5zy, then bd-sel (the bypass matrix should include the script forms above; I will take its entries from tests/script_files.rs rather than invent a second set).

title: Track A: replay harness (veil replay --audit) and warn-to-deny rollout

DESIGN: 'veil replay --audit ~/.cmdrvl/logs/veil/audit.jsonl [--since]' re-evaluates every Bash/Read/Grep entry that carries enough input (add raw tool_input capture to the audit schema in bd-5zy, hashed path only if [policy] audit_inputs=false) under the current rules and prints allow->deny and deny->allow flips grouped by rule, plus the top 20 commands that would newly deny. title: Implement path-based heuristic packs: credentials and compliance
description:
## Scope
Implement the built-in heuristic packs using path and filename conventions only, without opening file contents.

## Deliverables
- `core.credentials` for credentials-bearing config and token-like targets
- compliance-oriented packs for financial, PII, and HIPAA-style artifacts using path, filename, and extension heuristics
- clear pack metadata so `explain` style commands can report why a match occurred

## Out of Scope
- reading file contents
- registry and dispatch infrastructure
- path extraction
- evaluator policy resolution

## Acceptance Criteria
- unit tests cover representative positive and negative cases for each heuristic pack
- no pack requires opening or sampling file contents to classify a path
- false-positive guard cases are included for common safe files such as docs and source code
- pack ordering does not create unstable or conflicting results for the same path

title: Track A: directory-scope Grep and content search
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic.

PROBLEM: Grep tool with output_mode=content and path=data/ (a protected directory) is ALLOWED; only a file path is denied. Bash 'grep ssn data/x.csv', 'grep -r ssn data', 'rg ssn data/' are ALLOWED. Content-mode search is a raw read.

DESIGN: In src/evaluator.rs for the Grep tool: if output_mode is content (or unset? check Claude Code default: files_with_matches) and the path is a directory, deny when the directory is inside or contains any protected pattern root, or when any protected pattern glob could match a file under it. For Bash grep/rg/ag/ack/ugrep: treat as reader commands under the argv rule; -l / --files-with-matches / -c only -> allow with audit (names and counts, not content).

TESTS: Grep content on dir, on file, files_with_matches on dir; Bash grep -l vs grep; rg --files.
acceptance_criteria: Regression coverage shows protected-directory content searches and Bash grep/rg content reads denied, while filename/count-only searches remain metadata-only and audited.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-10-27 (validated, root-caused)
Problem: Grep content searches on directories and Bash grep/rg reads are not screened as file reads. Searching an ancestor of protected roots can therefore expose matching raw content to the agent.
Root cause: extract_grep_path extracts one path; evaluate_access checks only that exact path. SafePathMatcher's /** rule matches descendants, not ancestor directories. Bash command_paths recognizes cat/bat/less/more/head/tail but omits grep and rg. (src/extract.rs:126-146,251-257; src/evaluator.rs:88-98,217-223; src/allowlist.rs:134-145)
Validated: Static trace confirms omitted output_mode defaults to ReadsContents, but ancestor directories do not match protected roots and grep/rg yield no Bash candidates. Current main source matches local. This is under bd-30b Track A and blocks bd-1m2/bd-sel; no tests or live session run.
Evidence: src/extract.rs:126-146; src/extract.rs:251-257; src/evaluator.rs:88-98,217-223; src/allowlist.rs:134-145
Done when: Regression coverage shows protected-directory content searches and Bash grep/rg content reads denied, while filename/count-only searches remain metadata-only and audited.
Direction (hint, engineer decides): Match directory searches against protected roots beneath or above the supplied path, and extract grep-family argv paths with content-versus-metadata exposure.

Known gaps recorded in the bead, not claimed fixed: git grep, find -exec grep, xargs grep, sh -c grep, first-command-only pipelines (bd-sel / bd-vyk). Test assertions changed in d0169e9 only to the new, more accurate reason wording. ag/ack option tables from docs, unverified.

comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
EVIDENCE bd-1si (BrownChapel, 2026-11-25). Implemented and pushed; NOT closed. Commits on origin/main: 4e5d653 (feature), f37b633 (option tables checked against installed rg/ugrep).

ROOT CAUSE FIXED: only the exact path was checked and `dir/**` matches descendants, so a content search of an ancestor (or of the protected root itself) was allowed. Grep with no `path` extracted no candidate at all.

WHAT CHANGED
- src/allowlist.rs: SafePathMatcher::scan_directory(dir, max_entries) -> DirectoryScan::{Protected(path), Clear, Unverified}. Breadth-first walk; a directory is a protected root when a file placed in it would match (probe), which also covers the start directory; symlinks are not descended into but count when their target is covered (grep -R / rg -L); unreadable dirs skipped; budget exhaustion is Unverified, never Clear.
- src/evaluator.rs: before the allowlist, a ReadsContents access to an existing directory is walked (budget DIRECTORY_SCOPE_MAX_ENTRIES = 200,000) and denied through the normal policy mode (deny/warn/log) when anything covered sits beneath it, or when the directory cannot be inspected within the budget. The reason does not name the protected file.
- src/extract.rs: Grep with no/empty `path` = search of cwd; output_mode `count` is metadata-only like `files_with_matches`. Bash: grep/egrep/fgrep/zgrep family, ugrep/ug, rg, ag, ack parsed (option tables, pattern vs operands, recursion, metadata flags). Names/counts flags (-l -L -c -q, rg --files/-l/-c/--count-matches, ag -l/-c/-g, ack -l/-f/-g) => MetadataOnly. A recursive search with no operand (rg/ag/ack always, grep -r/-R/-d recurse, ugrep -r/-1..-9) searches cwd. -f/--file pattern files are content reads even with -l. A shell wildcard operand is kept literally and, when recursive, also as the directory before the wildcard.
- README.md: documents the behaviour and two limits.

ACCEPTANCE: "protected-directory content searches and Bash grep/rg content reads denied, while filename/count-only searches remain metadata-only and audited" -> MET for the forms listed above, shown by tests that run the real `veil` binary against real directories (tests/directory_scope.rs) plus unit tests with real temp trees.

EVIDENCE (re-executed at f37b633; working tree has only unrelated .beads/crates changes)
- cargo test --locked --lib --test directory_scope --test allowlist --test spine_denied_flags --test bare_invocation --test protected_corpus => 178 lib, 19 allowlist, 5 bare_invocation, 8 directory_scope, 19 protected_corpus, 6 spine_denied_flags passed, 0 failed.
- cargo clippy --locked --lib --bin veil --test directory_scope --no-deps -- -D warnings => exit 0. rustfmt --edition 2024 --check on my files clean.
- Mutation checks (each turned tests red, files restored byte-identical by md5): scan disabled in the evaluator => 6 evaluator + 4 directory_scope tests fail; short names/counts flags ignored => 2 extract + 1 directory_scope fail; Grep no-path default removed => 1 extract + 1 directory_scope fail.
- ubs: 3-4 "critical" per file set, all false positives in lines I did not write (allowlist.rs wildcard matcher `pattern[0] == b'*'`, evaluator.rs:940 and extract.rs:1500 pre-existing test asserts); nothing in new code. The pre-commit hook also staged .beads/issues.jsonl into 4e5d653 (br state of all agents), not a path I passed.
- Real tools: installed rg 15.2.0 and /usr/bin/grep (it is ugrep 7.8.4 on this machine) were run on a scratch dir: -l/-c/-L/-q/--files/--count-matches print names/counts only; `grep -r ssn .` and `rg ssn` print content, and rg with no path searches cwd even with a non-tty stdin. ag and ack are NOT installed: their option tables are from documentation and unchecked. ugrep rejects abbreviated long options; I did not test GNU grep (not installed).
- Hook latency (veil release build, one machine, scan of a content-searched directory, no protected data found): 26,528 entries 0.12 s warm / 1.2 s cold; at the 200,000-entry budget ~0.95 s warm / 2.9 s cold (a 1.7M-entry tree is refused at the budget). No walk happens when no `protected` patterns are configured, the access is not a content read, or the path is not a directory (one stat for a content read).

KNOWN GAPS (not fixed here)
1. Not recognised as searches: `git grep`, `find -exec grep`, `xargs grep`, `sh -c "grep ..."`, variables/`$(...)`/`~`/brace expansion in operands. Only the FIRST simple command of a pipeline is analysed and `&&`/`;` are not separators (pre-existing: `cd data && grep -r x .` or `cat x | grep` bypass). Belongs with the bypass matrix (bd-sel).
2. The Grep tool's `glob` and `type` filters are ignored, so a search of a directory that holds protected data is denied even if the filter would skip it; the agent must search a narrower path. Over-blocking, not under-blocking.
3. Directories over 200,000 entries are refused rather than assumed clean (a repo root with big node_modules/target and a protected dir configured will need a narrower path). Budget is a constant, not config.
4. Wildcard operands: without -r a wildcard expanding to a protected file is only caught when the literal text matches a pattern (same as `cat`). With a recursive search the directory before the wildcard is scanned, which can over-block (`rg pat *.rs` in a repo with a protected dir).
5. Built-in sensitivity packs (.env, keys) found beneath a searched directory are NOT considered; only `[sensitivity] protected` patterns are. `grep -r` reads .env; the Grep tool (ripgrep) skips hidden/ignored files by default, but veil walks everything.
6. Non-Claude protocols (Gemini grep_search, Copilot, Grok) use other argument names; they now get the cwd-scope check when `path` is absent but their own path argument (e.g. dir_path) is not read. Not tested.
7. Heredoc'd shell bodies (`bash <<EOF ... grep -l ...`) are treated as content reads, so names-only searches inside them are over-blocked.

comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
GAP FOUND (BrownChapel, checking the orchestrator's question): at HEAD 6923d2f a recursive search of a directory is allowed when the file inside is one veil denies BY NAME only because a built-in sensitivity pack recognises it. bd-1si's directory scan sees configured [sensitivity] protected patterns only. Reopening as instructed.

PROBE (debug binary built from this tree; isolated HOME/XDG/audit path; the hook payload is the PreToolUse Bash JSON on stdin; `.env` holds the dummy line SECRET=dummy-value-not-real)
Repo A: `.env` and `src/a.rs`, no `.veil.toml`. `.env` is protected only by the built-in packs.
Repo B: the same files plus `.veil.toml` with `[sensitivity] protected = [".env"]`.

                                     A (pack only)   B (configured pattern)
cat .env                             DENY            DENY
grep SECRET .env                     DENY            DENY
grep -r SECRET .                     allow  <-gap    DENY
rg SECRET .                          allow  <-gap    DENY
grep -r SECRET   (no path)           allow  <-gap    DENY
rg SECRET        (no path)           allow  <-gap    DENY
grep -rn SECRET ./                   allow  <-gap    DENY
find . -exec cat {} \;               allow  <-gap    DENY
find . -name .env -exec cat {} \;    allow  <-gap    DENY
grep -r SECRET src   (control)       allow           allow

ANSWER TO "only protected-directory patterns, or a gap?"
Both. bd-1si met its written acceptance criteria and triage text, which speak only of `[sensitivity] protected` patterns: repo B shows grep -r / rg / find -exec cat denied. But the guarantee an operator reads into it, "a file veil denies by name is also denied by a search of the directory that holds it", is false for every file that only a pack catches (.env, .ssh/, credentials, the financial/PII/HIPAA heuristics). The cause is in the code: evaluator.rs directory_scope_with calls matcher.scan_directory (SafePathMatcher, patterns only) and never consults the PackRegistry.

NOT bd-2mi's: `find . -exec cat {} \;` in repo A is this same gap (the root `.` is scanned and found clear). The other two probe vectors are bd-2mi's and are in flight: `ls -a | xargs cat` and `f=.env; cat $f` (both allowed in A and B at HEAD).

FIX SKETCH (not started; not mine to decide the cost)
Make the directory scan classify the entries it walks with the pack registry as well as the configured patterns, and stop skipping the scan when the configured list is short. Cost for the orchestrator to decide before this lands: the scan already gives up with "unverified" after max_entries and denies; once packs count, every `grep -r` of a large repository from its root hits that limit, whether or not the project configured anything. Options: (a) accept it, (b) pack-aware scan only for `.env`-class names found by a bounded walk and unverified = allow with an audit record, (c) a [policy] knob. I would take (b) with the knob, but it changes what "unverified" means for configured patterns, so it is a decision.

FAILING TEST
I will add the vector to tests/directory_scope.rs as an #[ignore = "bd-1si reopened: ..."] test (a committed failing test would turn main red), run it with `cargo test --test directory_scope -- --ignored`, and post the output in a follow-up comment. The test: repo A layout, commands `grep -r SECRET .`, `rg SECRET .`, `find . -exec cat {} \;`; each must be denied. It is not in the tree yet.

NOT VERIFIED: macOS only; the probe ran my debug binary, not a live Claude Code hook; I did not check what `rg --files` or `grep -l` do in repo A (they are names-only and should stay allowed).

comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
BrownChapel: answer to the orchestrator's check, with the failing test committed (8456a2a, pushed).

IT IS A GAP, not a protected-directory-only property.

Vector: a repo whose only secret is `.env`, which a built-in pack protects, with no `.veil.toml`. Run from the repo root (HEAD 8456a2a, macOS, scratch HOME and audit path):

    cat .env                    deny  (pack)
    grep -r SECRET .            ALLOW
    rg SECRET .                 ALLOW
    rg SECRET                   ALLOW
    find . -exec cat {} \;      ALLOW

Cause: `SafePathMatcher::scan_directory` (src/allowlist.rs) walks a searched directory looking for paths covered by `[sensitivity] protected` only. The built-in packs are classified per path by the evaluator, never by the walk, so a file only a pack recognises is invisible to it. With a `.veil.toml` that lists `.env` under `protected`, the same four commands are denied (checked in a second scratch repo).

Failing test, committed as ignored: `a_recursive_search_finds_a_file_only_a_builtin_pack_protects` in tests/directory_scope.rs. It first asserts `cat .env` is denied (so the gap is the walk and not the pack), then that the four commands are denied.

    running 1 test
    test a_recursive_search_finds_a_file_only_a_builtin_pack_protects ... FAILED
    panicked at tests/directory_scope.rs:490:5:
    these commands read `.env` and must be denied: ["grep -r SECRET .", "rg SECRET .", "rg SECRET", "find . -exec cat {} \\;"]
    test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 8 filtered out

The default `cargo test --test directory_scope` run stays green (8 passed, 1 ignored). Remove the `#[ignore]` when the walk consults the packs.

README now says so (Directory scope paragraph): the walk finds `[sensitivity] protected` paths only.

Reopening bd-1si is your call; I have not changed its status. bd-2mi's dynamic-argument stance does not close this: `find . -exec cat {} \;` has no unresolved word, and `grep -r SECRET .` names a literal directory.

title: Track A: MCP tool argument screening for protected paths
description:
Parent bd-30b. Depends on bd-29r (argv rule).

WHY: Claude Code fires PreToolUse for mcp__* tools as well. Cairn's send path (email/chat tools) passes attachment paths and file ids as string arguments. Today veil ignores non-Read/Grep/Bash tools entirely, so an agent can hand a protected file to a send-email MCP tool with no decision recorded. This is the mechanical form of bd-3mr / bd-37u.

DESIGN: In src/hook.rs, for any tool_name starting with mcp__ (and for Claude Code's WebFetch/NotebookRead style tools with path-like args), walk tool_input recursively; every string value that resolves to an existing path (absolute, ~, or relative to cwd) is screened with the argv rule; protected -> policy decision with class 'mcp_argument' and the JSON pointer of the offending field in the reason. Arrays of attachments handled. Non-path strings are never inspected for content (veil is a path guard). Config: [mcp] screen = true; [mcp] ignore_tools = [] for tools whose arguments are known not to be paths.

HOOK INSTALL: veil install adds a PreToolUse matcher for 'mcp__.*' (pipe-delimited alternation already supported since bd-nff). veil doctor checks it.

TESTS: fixtures for a send-email tool with attachments[] of protected paths, a file-upload tool with a single path, a non-path string that looks like a path but does not exist (allow), nested objects; hook install/uninstall idempotence with the new matcher.
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator at 5b8be2c: full suite 575 passed, 0 failed on clean export; CI green (df13845 and later). MCP tool argument screening for protected paths, real-binary tests with synthetic PreToolUse payloads. Gaps stated by the author and NOT claimed: NotebookRead/WebFetch-style tools not routed (recommend follow-up bead); directory args judged as one path; paths built inside strings (--file=x, @x, a.csv,b.csv) not found; project .veil.toml can set [mcp] screen=false like any setting; veil doctor now exits 1 until veil install is re-run. Not verified: live Claude Code session, independent review.

comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
bd-1wa evidence (BrownChapel). Commit df13845 on main; CI run 45681487052 green (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, ast-grep spine rules, doctor smoke). Not closing: needs an independent verifier.

WHAT LANDED
- Any tool named mcp__<server>__<tool> is ToolKind::Mcp; HookInput carries the real tool_name. src/mcp.rs walks tool_input (objects and arrays, RFC 6901 pointers) and judges each string that names a path with the same evaluator a command word goes through, as a non-spine tool.
- A string names a path when (a) it is rooted (/x, ~/x, file:///x, file://localhost/x) with no whitespace: judged whether or not the file exists, as a command word is; or (b) it is anything else (relative name, text with spaces) and lstat finds a file of that name under the agent's cwd (symlinks followed by the evaluator). Prose is never read for paths. Object keys, numbers, booleans and URLs (https://, s3://) are not judged.
- Denial reason names the tool and field: "(argument `/attachments/1`)". Audit record: real tool name, reason_class mcp_argument. `veil audit --class mcp_argument` lists them; cli value_parser and operator.json updated.
- Arguments deeper than 32 levels or with more than 10,000 strings are denied (policy default), because veil cannot show nothing in them is protected. Bulk tools need ignore_tools.
- Config: [mcp] screen (default true), ignore_tools (exact name or trailing *). Entries not starting with mcp__, with a non-trailing *, or with whitespace are config errors; unknown [mcp] keys are errors. Later layer replaces the earlier (ignore_tools is replaced, not merged).
- veil install writes an mcp__.* PreToolUse entry (MANAGED_MATCHERS). veil doctor has an mcp_hook check (error + `veil install` remediation when missing/invalid; ok when [mcp] screen = false). The matcher is NOT in REQUIRED_MATCHERS: operator preflight still needs only Read/Grep/Bash, so an older install is not locked out. A WebFetch|mcp__.* combined matcher counts as installed. uninstall removes it. install is idempotent (tests/doctor.rs runs install twice and compares settings).

AGAINST THE BEAD'S AC
- Send-email tool with attachments[] of protected paths: tests/mcp.rs (deny, pointer, audit record shape).
- File-upload tool with a single path: same file, 7 spellings (abs, relative, ~/, file://, padded with whitespace, .. segments, rooted nonexistent).
- Non-path string that looks like a path but does not exist: allowed (relative nonexistent), plus prose mentioning a protected path is allowed, plus a directory argument is allowed.
- Nested objects: /record/files/1/source/path; symlink to a protected file followed; path with spaces.
- Config: screen=false, ignore_tools exact and prefix, invalid entries, layering (src/config.rs unit tests).
- Install/uninstall idempotence, doctor check: src/hooks.rs unit tests, src/operator.rs unit tests, tests/doctor.rs real-CLI tests (install then doctor healthy; pre-MCP install: operator command still runs, doctor exits 1 with mcp_hook error, preflight posture still healthy, install closes it).

VERIFICATION RUN (clean copy = git archive of a44cea2 overlaid with my 13 files, because the shared tree does not compile while another agent's uncommitted extract work is in flight; the commit is exactly those 13 files on a44cea2, HEAD did not move)
- cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast: 571 tests across 16 targets, 0 failed (lib 323, bin 79, tests/mcp.rs 13, tests/doctor.rs 17, others unchanged). rustfmt --edition 2024 --check clean. clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean. ubs on changed files: only the known false-positive "secret compared with ==" criticals in code I did not touch (evaluator.rs, lib.rs STDIN_ARGUMENTS match); my one panic! in a test helper was rewritten to assert!.
- Mutation checks, each applied to the clean copy and reverted; each fails the tests meant to catch it: never screen (10 of 13 mcp tests fail); pointer dropped (4); relative name judged without a file (5 unit + 1 integration); no trim (2); no ~ expansion (3); no file:// (2); depth limit off (2); ignore_tools never consulted (2 integration + 1 unit); screen layering ignored (unit + operator); reason class reported as argv_path (4 + audit test); lstat replaced by stat (dangling-symlink unit test); MCP matcher made required (9 doctor/hooks tests); MCP matcher not installed (8, plus both real-CLI doctor tests); doctor check removed (4).
- Cost, debug build, real binary: 10,000 non-rooted strings 50-75 ms; 10,000 distinct rooted paths about 450 ms (full evaluation each). Not measured in release.

GAPS, NOT HIDDEN
1. Bead says "and WebFetch/NotebookRead style tools with path-like args". Not done: only mcp__* is routed to veil. NotebookRead takes a notebook_path and is not covered by the Read matcher either, so a protected .ipynb read through it is unseen. Needs its own matcher and tool-kind decision; I recommend a follow-up bead (P1 if notebooks are in scope for protected data).
2. Behaviour change: veil doctor now exits 1 on any install without the mcp__.* entry until `veil install` is re-run. Preflight is unchanged. If you would rather doctor report it as a warning, say so.
3. Directory arguments are judged as one path, not scanned: an MCP tool handed the project root is allowed even though it holds a protected file.
4. Relative names resolve against the agent's cwd; an MCP server running elsewhere may resolve the same string to a different file.
5. Paths built inside a string are not found: --file=x.csv, a.csv,b.csv, @x.csv, percent-escaped file:// URLs. veil judges what the agent hands the tool, not what the tool does with ids or on its own.
6. Rooted nonexistent paths ARE judged (bead says "existing path"): a protected-directory path that does not exist is denied, matching how a command word is treated. Deliberate: a command word is judged the same way, and a path inside a protected directory is protected whether or not the file is there yet. It does mean a tool handed a not-yet-existing path in a protected directory is denied.
7. A project .veil.toml can set [mcp] screen = false, like any setting; the project layer overrides the user layer.
8. Arguments past 32 levels or 10,000 strings are denied; legitimate bulk tools need ignore_tools.
9. Verified only by me, on macOS, against a clean copy; the real-binary tests drive the hook with synthetic payloads in the Claude Code PreToolUse shape, not a live Claude Code session. No independent verifier has run this.
10. The repo commit hook added the shared .beads/issues.jsonl (other agents' bead edits) to df13845.

title: Extract candidate paths from simple Bash read commands
description:
## Scope
Extract candidate file paths from simple Bash read commands that name files directly.

## Deliverables
- support for direct file-reading commands such as `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `less`, `more`, and `bat`
- quoted path handling
- multiple file argument handling
- simple pipe handling where the left side reads a file and later stages post-process output

## Out of Scope
- heredocs
- inline interpreter snippets such as `python -c` and `node -e`
- path hardening after extraction

## Acceptance Criteria
- unit tests cover direct commands, quoted paths, multiple file arguments, and simple piped forms
- non-read commands such as `ls`, `git`, and `cd` return zero candidates
- false positives are avoided for commands that inspect metadata without reading file contents

title: Track B: broker daemon and veil exec client
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic. Depends on B1.

WHAT: 'veil sandbox' starts a broker (same binary, --broker mode) listening on a per-session unix socket under ~/.cmdrvl/state/veil/broker/<session>.sock (0600). Protocol: newline-delimited JSON {"tool":"shape","argv":[...],"cwd":...}; never a shell string. Broker checks tool basename against [spine] authorized_tools, resolves the binary via PATH captured at launch, refuses argv containing shell metacharacters that would need a shell, runs it with the operator's real permissions, streams {stream, chunk} frames and a final {exit_code}. Every call is audit-logged with enforcement:'sandbox', origin:'broker'.

CLIENT: 'veil exec <tool> [args]' inside the sandbox; also honor VEIL_BROKER_SOCKET. Hook remediation text inside a sandbox says 'run: veil exec shape <path>'.

SECURITY: the broker is the only privileged path; keep it tiny, no config reload, dies with the sandbox parent (SIGHUP/pidfd). Rate-limit and size-cap output (spine tools emit metadata; 16 MiB cap).

TESTS: protocol unit tests; integration test launching broker + client with a fake 'shape' script; rejection tests (unauthorized tool, shell metachars, path escape).

AMBITION ROUND ADDITIONS (2026-09-02): (a) FLAG POLICY: each authorized tool declares flags that raise its output label to protected (shape --explicit, rvl --raw, profile --dump, canon --show-values); the broker refuses them with reason broker_flag_forbidden. Without this the broker is cat with extra steps. Config: [spine.flags] shape = ["--explicit"] etc., with built-in defaults for the cmdrvl spine tools. (b) OUTPUT SCANNING: before returning stdout the broker runs the shared boundary-detectors packs (crate extracted in airlock bead al-34s; pinned dependency) and refuses (default) or redacts output that trips secrets/PII/tabular-dump detectors, recording the refusal with detector id and span hash. (c) DERIVED REGISTRY: every returned output (and any file the tool wrote under --out) is hashed and appended to ~/.cmdrvl/state/veil/derived.jsonl {hash, tool, argv_hash, session, ts}; the provenance allowlist bead consumes this. (d) LINUX: apply a seccomp filter to the sandboxed tree denying ptrace, process_vm_readv/writev and opening /proc/<pid>/mem so an adversarial agent cannot read broker memory; macOS relies on seatbelt's default debugging denial - document.

REFINEMENT ROUND 1 (2026-09-02): deliver 'veil exec <tool> [args]' DIRECT MODE first (no sandbox, no socket): validates tool + flag policy, runs the tool, scans output with boundary-detectors, registers output hashes in derived.jsonl, audits. This gives Track A the derived registry (bd-3qw) without waiting for the sandbox; the broker daemon is the same code path behind a socket. Step order: 1 direct mode, 2 socket protocol, 3 daemon lifecycle.
notes:
2026-11-24 review notes:
- Reuse the `[spine.denied_flags]` table from the P0 hook-mode flag guard (`--explicit`, `--raw`, `--dump`, `--show-values`) so hook and broker enforce identical flag policies.
- Scan broker stdout with the shared `boundary-detectors` crate before returning frames to the sandboxed agent (including recursive base64/hex decode-and-rescan).
- Concurrency/runtime: broker daemon may stay tiny sync thread-per-connection OR use `asupersync` for cancel-correct streaming & parent-death teardown; NEVER pull an async runtime into `veil` hook mode (<1ms startup budget).
close_reason: Verified at 10bf694: CI run 45746128157 green, incl. macos-seatbelt-sandbox running all 6 tests/sandbox.rs tests; local 814 passed at 45d8c08. Operator approved moving two unbuilt requirements ('agree on your recommendations', 2026-11-25): Linux seccomp to bd-34r; hashing --out files in direct mode to bd-3qw. Neither is built. This session's security fixes have had no second reviewer.

comments.author: zacharyruiz
comments.text: Design before implementation: keep hook mode as the default; Track B uses the ADR B-1 opt-in sandbox with a narrow broker started outside OS confinement. Load the same merged Config as hook evaluation. Authorize exact configured spine tool names and reuse `src/spine.rs` `DeniedFlags::find` (including default + per-tool flags); refuse a configured raw-output flag before spawn. Each allowlisted tool must have an explicit output-class contract; return only public/derived output, and refuse protected-class output. Scan stdout with boundary-detectors as a secondary check, then hash the typed request and returned bytes for audit/derived registration without logging raw values. Transport is newline-delimited typed JSON `{tool, argv}` (validated cwd only if needed), never a shell string; resolve the executable using PATH captured when the broker starts and execute argv directly. Use a private 0700 session directory and 0600 session socket, cap request/frame sizes, 16 MiB output per call, and a finite per-session call count; terminate the broker when its launcher exits. Test the real client under the compiled macOS Seatbelt profile: direct protected-file read must fail while `veil exec shape <protected-file>` returns only derived metadata; also cover unauthorized tool, denied flags, malformed/oversize request, scanner hit, and output cap. Claim attempt is currently rejected by beads because bd-27o still depends on bd-jg9 (IN_PROGRESS), despite bd-e6v now CLOSED; no broker code changed yet.

title: Track A: path-anywhere-in-argv rule replaces the reader allowlist
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic.

PROBLEM: src/extract.rs only recognizes cat/bat/less/more/head/tail plus a few interpreters. awk 1 data/x.csv, sed -n p data/x.csv, base64/xxd/perl/jq/sqlite3/duckdb/grep/rg on a protected file are all ALLOWED (probe 2026-09-02). So are cp/tar/curl -F file=@ which move the bytes somewhere unguarded.

DESIGN: After shell decomposition (sibling bead), for every simple command: resolve each argv token that looks like a path (contains / or a known file extension, or resolves to an existing file relative to cwd) to an absolute path. If any resolved path is protected/sensitive under the existing classification, the command is resolved through policy UNLESS the command basename is in [spine] authorized_tools. The old reader list stays only as an explanation hint ('cat is a direct reader'). Keep the existing fast path: commands with no path-like tokens are allowed silently.

EDGE CASES: tokens like 2>/dev/null and dir> currently get logged as paths (see audit log) - the shell decomposer must strip redirections before argv resolution and treat '< protected' as a read (already denied). Ignore /dev/*, /proc/*. Never stat more than 64 tokens per command (perf budget < 1ms).

REASON CLASSES: add 'argv_path' to the audit reason vocabulary so operators can distinguish direct readers from generic path references.

TESTS: unit tests per vector in the bypass matrix bead; golden fixtures for awk/sed/jq/base64/xxd/perl/sqlite3/duckdb/cp/tar/curl/scp/rsync/zip; false-positive guards: 'ls data/', 'wc -l data/x.csv' (policy decision: wc leaks counts only - ALLOW with audit), 'shape data/x.csv' allowed, 'git add data/x.csv' allowed (not a read into context).

AMBITION ROUND ADDITIONS (2026-09-02): (a) Protected-pattern matching moves to a segment radix trie with glob leaves (src/allowlist.rs + src/config.rs) so 10k patterns still resolve in < 1 ms; add a criterion-free timing test with 10k synthetic patterns. (b) Frame decisions in the label model from docs/plan.md 'Formal model': files carry public < derived < protected; the agent's clearance is derived; this rule is 'protected path referenced by a non-broker command'. Reason strings should say which label was hit.

GitHub CI on 6923d2f success. Independent probe of HEAD with 21 vectors: 18 denied (awk, sed, jq, base64, xxd, sqlite3, cp, tar|base64, python -c, curl -F, scp, cat < ...); still ALLOWED: find -exec cat {}, xargs cat {}, f=.env; cat $f (bd-2mi dynamic-arg stance, open) and grep -r/rg on a dir (query on bd-1si). Not verified: lib unit tests locally, label-model wording in reason strings.

comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
EVIDENCE bd-29r (BrownChapel) — implemented at 2914df8, with a README/timing-test correction at cb5aa58; both pushed to origin/main. NOT closing; orchestrator verifies.

WHAT CHANGED
Every simple command that is not a known reader (cat bat less more head tail, grep family) is now judged by the path-shaped words it carries, after bd-2kr's decomposition and unwrapping. A protected path is resolved through policy unless the command is an authorized spine tool (SpineInvocation::for_path; a denied raw flag still denies). The reader list stays, but only to pick which parser runs; those commands keep reason_class direct_read.
Words that count as paths: a slash or a data-file extension; a bare word that exists on disk (symlink, directory); the value of --opt=v and key=@v; the tail after a colon (git show HEAD:x, scp host:x); quoted literals inside a longer word (select * from 'x.csv'); attached short-option values (sed -fPATH); the program word if it contains a slash. The script word of a shell is skipped; after `--` dash words are operands.
Exposure: ls wc stat du find mkdir touch rm echo git add/rm/status/commit/... name paths without reading them, so they stay allowed (ALLOW, no record for silent allows, as the bead's fast path asks). Everything else reads contents. A directory named to cp/mv/tar/zip/rsync/scp/curl/docker etc. is scanned like a content search; other commands treat it as a name (python3 -m pytest . stays allowed).
Redirections are dropped; the word after a BARE operator is kept so `cut -d '>' -f1 data/x.csv` cannot hide the file. `< path` is still a direct read. /dev and /proc are ignored except the descriptor paths the evaluator already blocks.
Audit gets reason_class: direct_read | argv_path. Denials name the command and the label: "`awk` names a path matched by data.tabular (label: protected) and is not an authorized spine tool, so it is blocked by policy default".

ACCEPTANCE, ITEM BY ITEM
- Bypass vectors denied: awk sed jq base64 xxd perl sqlite3 duckdb cp mv tar zip rsync scp curl (-F file=@x), plus dirs to cp -r/tar/zip/rsync/scp: tests/argv_path.rs::commands_veil_never_knew_as_readers_are_denied_for_naming_a_protected_file and a_whole_directory_handed_to_a_copy_or_archive_command_is_denied. MET.
- False-positive guards: ls data/, wc -l data/x.csv (ALLOW with audit), shape data/x.csv, git add data/x.csv stay allowed: ...::commands_that_only_name_a_protected_path_to_list_count_or_stage_it_stay_allowed. MET.
- Fast path (no path-like tokens → silent allow, no audit): ...::commands_that_name_nothing_protected_are_untouched_and_unaudited. MET.
- Redirections stripped, `< protected` still denied, /dev /proc ignored: ...::redirections_are_not_paths_but_a_quoted_operator_cannot_hide_the_file, ...::device_and_process_paths_are_not_files_to_protect_except_the_blocked_descriptors. MET.
- Reason class argv_path in audit: ...::the_audit_log_tells_a_direct_reader_from_a_path_named_in_the_words. MET.
- At most 64 words touch the filesystem: extract::tests::at_most_sixty_four_words_are_resolved_against_the_filesystem and ...::only_the_first_sixty_four_words_touch_the_filesystem_but_a_protected_path_past_them_is_denied. MET (a certain-shaped word past 64 is compared lexically; a bare word past 64 is dropped — see LIMITS).
- (b) Label in reason strings ("label: protected"): ...::the_denial_names_the_command_and_the_label_and_is_not_the_direct_read_message. MET as reason text only; no label type was added to the code.
- (a) Pattern index with 10k-pattern timing test: PARTLY MET, see below.
- Perf budget <1 ms per command: MET for typical commands (about 80 us for two files), NOT RELIABLY MET at the 64-word maximum (0.75–1.06 ms), see below.

PERFORMANCE (release, CARGO_TARGET_DIR in scratchpad; run with --nocapture)
- allowlist::tests::ten_thousand_patterns_resolve_a_command_worth_of_paths_inside_a_millisecond: 10k patterns, build 5.58 ms, 64 lookups 63 us, trying every pattern 27.6 ms (about 435x). The commit message says 56 us / 24 ms from an earlier run; this re-run is the one to trust.
- lib::tests::a_command_that_names_sixty_four_files_is_judged_in_about_a_millisecond (63 clean words + awk, 1 pattern): whole 0.75–0.99 ms over four runs, then 1.03–1.06 ms over three later runs on the same machine (extract ~0.4–0.5 ms + evaluate ~0.4–0.5 ms). Debug build 2.8 ms. Same test, a command naming two files: 79–82 us (three runs).
- lib::tests::ten_thousand_protected_patterns_do_not_slow_a_command_by_the_number_of_patterns (same command, 10k patterns, end to end): 4.2–4.9 ms release, 13.6 ms debug.
- Before the two perf fixes made late in this bead (per-directory cache + one lstat per word in ArgvResolver; one PathView per classification instead of one per pack) the 64-word command took 3.2 ms; after, 0.75–0.99 ms.
Honest gaps against the bead's numbers:
 1. The 10k-pattern <1 ms target holds for lookups (63 us) but NOT end to end: the index is built once per hook run (5.6 ms), so a hook call with 10k patterns costs about 4.5 ms in total. A prebuilt/cached index across hook runs would be a new bead; I did not file one.
 2. The 64-word command is NOT reliably under the bead's 1 ms: 0.75–0.99 ms on four runs, 1.03–1.06 ms on the last three. The bead's budget is met for commands of up to a few dozen words, not for the 64-word maximum. The asserted bound in the test is looser than the bead (3 ms release, 20 ms debug) so the test does not flake on a busy machine; that is a weaker assertion than the acceptance text, and the measurement is printed in the test output. I did not find a way to get the extraction (a lstat per word) lower without dropping the symlink check.
 3. The bead says the trie goes in "src/allowlist.rs + src/config.rs". src/config.rs is unchanged; the index lives in allowlist.rs only. It is a component trie for exact paths and dir/** plus literal-keyed buckets for globs, not a radix trie.
 4. A command that names two files takes about 80 us (measured late; the first README text said "a tenth" of the 64-word figure before that was measured, and a follow-up commit replaces it with the measurement).

SafePathMatcher still has to answer exactly like the old linear scan, quirks included (pattern "/" matches everything; dir/** does not match dir itself; a PathGlob is anchored at the start). Held by allowlist::tests::the_index_agrees_with_trying_every_pattern_on_random_patterns_and_paths (differential against the retained test-only linear oracle) and ...::the_index_keeps_the_quirks_of_the_patterns_as_written.

COMMANDS RUN (all green at 2914df8; after cb5aa58, which only touched README.md and the timing test in src/lib.rs, I re-ran rustfmt --check, clippy -D warnings and the lib tests (237 passed), not the integration suites)
rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <changed files>: ok
cargo clippy --locked --lib --bin veil --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings: exit 0
cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast, targeted: lib 237, bin 68, allowlist 22, argv_path 11, bare_invocation 5, directory_scope 8, doctor 15, golden_rules 15, operator_manifest 10, path_decision 9, protected_corpus 19, shell_decomposition 7, spine_denied_flags 6. 0 failed. (Not the whole workspace. The untracked crates/ was already there at session start; I did not touch it.)
Mutation checks, 8 of them (M1–M5, M7–M9; there was no M6): each made at least one targeted test fail, and each was reverted with the file restored byte-identical (md5 before/after). These ran BEFORE the late perf changes (ArgvResolver, shared PathView, canonical-path flag); after those I re-ran the full targeted set above, not the mutations.
ubs on the 9 changed files: Critical 5, Warning ~870. Three criticals are displayed: allowlist.rs:569 `pattern[0] == b'*'` and :580 `*first == pattern[0]` (both pre-existing wildcard matcher lines, present at 9d72d77) and extract.rs:196 `exposure == PathExposure::ReadsContents` (new in this bead; an enum compare). All three are "secret compared with ==" false positives on ordinary comparisons. ubs does not display the other two, so I have NOT checked those; I did not triage the warnings beyond reading the path-join and temp-file ones, which are test fixtures and the audit appender.

NEW FALSE POSITIVES THIS INTRODUCES (all intended, none silenced)
- A bare word that happens to name an existing protected file or directory in cwd is judged (tests: `awk 1 shortcut`, a symlink without an extension pointing at the protected file, is denied; `sort notes.md` is allowed).
- A command that reads contents and names any protected path is denied even if the command could not read it (e.g. a flag value). Warn mode (bd-1m2) is the intended valve.
- `git diff`/`git show`/`git log -p` of a protected path are denied as content reads (by the exposure table: only the subcommands in GIT_NAMES_ONLY_SUBCOMMANDS are names-only; I have no end-to-end test for those three); `git add/status/ls-files` stay allowed.
- A wildcard word (`awk 1 data/*.csv`) also names the directory it starts from, when the command reads.

LIMITS (not met, or deliberately out of scope)
- Redirection asymmetry: `> data/out.csv` (space) is denied because the word after a bare operator is kept; `>data/out.csv` (attached) is dropped and ALLOWED. A write is not a read, but a redirection onto a protected path is not judged as a write. A test pins the current behavior; it is not a decision, it is an open question for the egress bead (bd-x8o).
- Words past 64 per command: a certain-shaped word is compared with the protected patterns as text only (no symlink resolution), a bare word is dropped. A protected symlink named 65th by a bare name is a bypass.
- cwd tracking across cd/pushd/-C is bd-vyk; dynamic arguments ($VAR, $(...) results) are bd-2mi. Neither is addressed here, so `cd data && awk 1 x.csv` and `awk 1 $f` are still not judged by the argv rule beyond what bd-2kr's opaque handling already does.
- Inline scripts (python -c "open('x.csv')") are still found by the existing candidate extraction, not by the new rule.
- No content sniffing, no magic-byte or double-extension handling (bd-35u, bd-28k, bd-r93).
- The bypass-matrix bead (bd-sel) is not done; tests/argv_path.rs has golden vectors for the tools listed above (source lines per tool: awk 27, cp 7, tar 6, curl 5, sed 4, jq 3, rsync 3, sqlite3 2, duckdb 2, scp 2, zip 2, base64/xxd/perl 1 each) but is not that committed matrix.
- Not verified on Linux; developed and tested on macOS only (/tmp canonicalizes to /private/tmp there, which already broke three of my test expectations; I moved those to /srv).

API ADDITIONS (public to the crate): CommandExtraction.{argv_paths, argv_exposure, argv_scans_directories}; EvaluationInput.{argv_command, scan_directories, canonical} with_argv_command / with_canonical_path; evaluator::PolicyMatchers (built once per hook run); pub(crate) evaluator::is_blocked_device_path; SpineInvocation::for_path; audit record key reason_class (README documents it); ClassificationRequest is no longer Copy (it carries the PathView).

PROCESS NOTES
- Commit message says "12 real-binary tests in tests/argv_path.rs"; there are 11. Cannot amend (no amend rule); this comment is the correction.
- The pre-commit hook staged .beads/issues.jsonl into the code commit (2 lines), as before.
- Late perf edits touched src/packs/mod.rs (reserved by me, released below) beyond the file list I first reserved.
- No scripts rewrote code; every edit was by hand with the Edit tool.

title: Detect inline-script and heredoc file reads in Bash input
description:
## Scope
Detect file reads hidden inside heredocs and inline interpreter snippets in Bash tool input.

## Deliverables
- detection for heredoc-fed file reads and redirects
- detection for inline interpreters such as `python -c`, `node -e`, `perl -e`, and `ruby -e`
- extraction of candidate file paths from these forms when they read files

## Out of Scope
- simple direct read commands already covered by the basic Bash extractor
- evaluator policy decisions
- path hardening after extraction

## Acceptance Criteria
- golden-style tests cover heredoc, `python -c`, `node -e`, `perl -e`, and `ruby -e` examples
- safe commands such as `echo`, `mkdir`, and `git status` do not produce false positives
- nested quoting edge cases are handled without panic

title: Track C: twin mode - synthetic look-alike data in place of protected directories
description:
Parent bd-30b. Depends on bd-34r (sandbox launcher). Related to the twinning tooling used for warehouse eval packs (cmdrvl skills).

WHY: README's 'Zero-Retention Mode' says the agent never touches the documents and only writes a pipeline the client runs. Nothing enforces it. Twin mode makes it mechanical and demoable.

DESIGN: 'veil sandbox --twin [--twin-dir DIR] -- claude': for each protected directory, generate (or reuse from DIR) a synthetic twin with the same relative file names and, where a generator exists (CSV/TSV/parquet/JSON via the twinning toolkit; opaque bytes otherwise), the same schema with fabricated values; bind-mount / symlink the twin over the protected path inside the sandbox (macOS: seatbelt path rewrite is not available, so use a per-session overlay directory and set cwd + VEIL_TWIN_ROOT, with the real path denied; Linux: mount namespace bind). The agent develops against the twin; 'veil exec' runs the frozen script on real data via the broker on operator request. Session attestation (Track D) records twin=true and that zero real bytes were readable.

TESTS: twin generation determinism (seeded); agent-side read of the real path denied; script developed on twin runs via broker on fixture real data; e2e script with logging.
notes:
2026-11-24 review notes (warehouse/DB twin integration with `cmdrvl/twinning`):
- Extend `veil sandbox --twin` beyond local file overlays to also support `cmdrvl/twinning` synthetic database/warehouse endpoints: start/connect a local `twinning` Postgres/Snowflake twin, inject `DATABASE_URL` / `PGHOST` / `PGPORT` / `SNOWFLAKE_*` into the sandboxed harness, while sandbox network rules block real production warehouse egress.
- Enables a sealed zero-retention data-engineering workstation where agents develop and test real SQL/dbt/Rust pipelines against a faithful twin without ever touching production rows or real files.

- downstream command beads can add behavior without reworking top-level CLI structure

title: Track A: shell decomposition and wrapper unwrapping
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic. Blocks the argv rule bead (the rule needs simple commands as input).

PROBLEM: 'sh -c "cat data/x.csv"', 'find data -type f -exec cat {} \;', 'ls data | xargs -I{} cat data/{}', 'echo $(cat data/x.csv)', 'uv run python -c ...' are all ALLOWED because extraction only looks at the top-level command.

DESIGN: In src/extract.rs add a decomposer that turns a Bash tool command string into a list of simple commands: split on ; && || | newline; recurse into $( ... ) and backticks; unwrap -c strings for sh/bash/zsh/dash; unwrap wrappers env, nice, nohup, time, timeout, sudo, doas, xargs (treat remaining argv as the command; -I{} placeholders become dynamic args), find -exec/-execdir (the exec argv is a simple command with {} dynamic), uv run, uvx, pipx run, poetry run, pdm run, npx, bunx, deno run. Use shlex (already a dependency) per segment; on shlex failure treat the whole string as one opaque command and fall through to the dynamic-arg stance. Depth cap 8, segment cap 64.

OUTPUT: Vec<SimpleCommand { argv, redirects_in, has_dynamic_args, origin: 'top'|'subshell'|'wrapper' }>. Evaluate every simple command; first deny wins; audit logs every evaluated segment with origin.

TESTS: table-driven unit tests for each wrapper; nested cases (sh -c "find . -exec cat {} \;"); quoting torture (cat da""ta/x.csv already denied - keep); perf test asserting < 1ms for a 4 KiB command string.
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator at c42a157 (clean git-archive export): tests/shell_decomposition.rs 7 passed, tests/directory_scope.rs 8 passed, 0 failed. bead TESTS covered: 18+17 unit tests in src/extract/{decompose,wrappers}.rs (CI Run tests success on 03ba37c, which includes them; I did not re-run the lib unit tests locally), nested cases in shell_decomposition, and the 4 KiB < 1 ms perf assertion at decompose.rs:1102. directory_scope.rs edits are doc comments only. Not verified: live Claude Code hook behavior. Pane filed bd-vyk for cwd tracking.

comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
bd-2kr evidence — BrownChapel — commit c42a157 (pushed to origin/main). Not closed; awaiting orchestrator verification.

WHAT CHANGED
The hook used to judge only the first simple command of a Bash tool call. It now splits the string into the commands that would run and evaluates each one.
- src/extract/decompose.rs (new): scanner + `decompose(&str) -> Vec<SimpleCommand>`. Splits on ; & && || | and newline; descends into $( ), backticks and <( ) / >( ); attaches here-documents (expanding bodies are scanned for $( ) too); strips leading assignments and compound-command keywords. `SimpleCommand { argv, redirects_in, has_dynamic_args, origin: top|subshell|wrapper }` as the bead specifies, plus `stdin_piped` and `heredoc_body`.
- src/extract/wrappers.rs (new): replaces env, nice, nohup, time, timeout, sudo, doas, exec, command, builtin, xargs, uv run, uvx, uv tool run, pipx run, poetry run, pdm run, npx, bunx, deno run with the command they run; runs sh/bash/zsh/dash/ksh/ash/fish/csh/tcsh `-c` strings, `eval`, `sudo -s`, `npx -c`, here-strings and heredocs fed to a shell back through the decomposer; turns `find ... -exec|-execdir|-ok|-okdir` into the command with `{}` replaced by each find root.
- src/extract.rs: `extract_bash_commands(command, cwd) -> Vec<CommandExtraction>` replaces the single-extraction `extract_bash_read_paths` (the old single-command helpers, the heredoc parser and the pipeline cutter are gone). rg/ag/ack fed by a pipe now search the pipe, not the working directory.
- src/lib.rs: each command is evaluated on its own; first deny wins; an authorized spine tool authorizes only the command that names it (`shape a; cat b` denies the cat); each evaluated path is audited with its origin.
- src/spine.rs: `detect_spine_argv` (per-command); src/audit.rs: `origin` field on every audit record.
- README.md: new paragraphs on what is followed and what is not. tests/directory_scope.rs: stale gap comment updated.
- Why child modules, not inline in extract.rs: the bead says "in src/extract.rs"; the decomposer and tables are ~2,000 lines with tests, so they live in src/extract/ and are re-exported from extract.

ACCEPTANCE (the bead's DESIGN / OUTPUT / TESTS)
- Separators, $( ), backticks, -c unwrap, every listed wrapper, find -exec/-execdir, xargs with -I{} placeholders flagged dynamic, shlex per segment, depth cap 8, segment cap 64: DONE.
- Evaluate every simple command, first deny wins, audit with origin: DONE. Caveat: audit records are per evaluated PATH, as before; a command that reaches no path writes no record.
- Table-driven unit tests per wrapper, nested `sh -c "find . -exec cat {} \;"`, `cat da""ta/x.csv` stays denied, 4 KiB timing: DONE (see below).
- Timing (min of 50 runs, adversarial 4 KiB inputs the segment cap allows; `cargo test --lib four_kib -- --nocapture`): debug build 443 µs and 223 µs for 4,082 and 3,768 bytes with --test-threads=1; release build 240 µs and 136 µs. Under load from other agents' builds the debug test still passed. The bound asserted is 1 ms.
- Not done, by design of the bead's dependents: the dynamic-argument stance. `has_dynamic_args` is computed and unit-tested but nothing in veil branches on it yet (consumer: bd-2mi).

WHAT IS STILL ALLOWED (pinned where a test can pin it)
- Unparseable text (unbalanced quote or substitution, trailing backslash), more than 8 levels of nesting, more than 64 segments, and a wrapper chain longer than 8 come back as an opaque command that is allowed. tests/shell_decomposition.rs pins "segment 65 is allowed, segment 64 is denied" and the unbalanced-quote case, so closing them is a deliberate change (bd-2mi).
- Variables and other expansions (`f=data/x.csv; cat $f`): allowed, pinned.
- Not followed at all: `echo '...' | sh` (script on stdin from a pipe), `source`/`.`, `git grep`, `docker exec`, `ssh host cmd`, and every other command-runner not in the list. For bd-sel's matrix.
- A `cd`/`pushd`/`-C` earlier in the line: relative paths still resolve against the hook's directory. Filed bd-vyk (P1) with the concrete under-block (`cd data && cat clients/x.csv`, true before this change) and the new over-block it can cause.
- Wrapper option tables: checked against the installed tool for uv run, uvx, pipx run, npx/npm exec, bunx, GNU timeout, and the BSD env, xargs, nice and find man pages. NOT checked (not installed, or not run): sudo, doas, poetry, pdm, deno. A value-taking option missing from a table makes its value look like the command, which hides the real one; that is the unsafe direction.

BEHAVIOR CHANGES A REVIEWER SHOULD KNOW
- Commands after the first one in a line, and after a pipe, are now evaluated. That blocks real bypasses and also adds new denials: `find . -name '*.rs' -exec grep -n x {} +` at a repo root holding protected paths is denied, because `{}` is treated as a content read of the root (-name/-type/-prune are ignored, as the Grep glob filter was in bd-1si). `cd /elsewhere && rg token` is denied if the repo root holds protected paths (bd-vyk).
- `uv run shape data/x.csv` and `sh -c "shape data/x.csv"` are now recognised as the authorized spine tool (before they were not recognised and read nothing, so were allowed either way).
- Public API: `extract_bash_read_paths` is removed in favour of `extract_bash_commands`; `detect_spine_invocation` stays (config.rs tests use it) and `detect_spine_argv` is added; `AuditRecord` has a new `origin` field (JSON key `origin`, always set: "top" for Read and Grep).

EVIDENCE (re-executed)
- `cargo test --locked --lib --bin veil --test shell_decomposition --test directory_scope --test spine_denied_flags --test path_decision --test operator_manifest --test golden_rules --test doctor --test bare_invocation --test allowlist`: lib 221, bin 68, shell_decomposition 7, directory_scope 8, spine_denied_flags 6, path_decision 9, operator_manifest 10, golden_rules 15, doctor 15, bare_invocation 5, allowlist 19; all passed. The 43 extract tests that existed before this change pass unchanged (a test-module adapter flattens the new per-command result so their call sites did not change). Not run: protected_corpus and the full suite.
- tests/shell_decomposition.rs runs the real binary against real files: 50 bypass forms denied with an evaluator reason; 25 clean or metadata-only forms allowed; spine scoping (7 stay authorized, 8 are denied); audit origins `top/subshell/wrapper` with decisions; the pinned gaps.
- Differential test: for plain commands the decomposer's argv equals `shlex::split` exactly.
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on all touched .rs files: clean. `cargo clippy --locked --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings` and `--lib --bin veil`: clean. `ubs` on the touched files: 0 critical except the old false positive at src/extract.rs `candidates[0] == fd_path` in an fd test (a path compare, not a secret); I renamed a `secret` variable in the new test file that ubs flagged.
- Mutation checks, each restored byte-identical (md5 compared) and each caught:
  M1 `;` not a separator -> 11 lib tests fail.
  M2 `-c` scripts not run -> 9 lib tests and 3 integration tests fail.
  M3 find `{}` not replaced by the root -> 5 lib tests and the integration bypass test fail.
  M4 spine taken from the first command for every command -> `an_authorized_spine_tool_authorizes_only_its_own_command` fails.
  M5 audit origin hard-coded to "top" -> the audit test fails.
  M6 piped rg/ag/ack search the working directory -> a lib test and the integration clean-forms test fail.

title: Track A: dynamic-argument stance (variables, globs, placeholders)
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic. Depends on shell decomposition.

PROBLEM: 'f=data/clients.csv; cat $f' is ALLOWED because $f is opaque. Same for xargs {} and find {} placeholders.

DESIGN: (1) Track simple assignments within the same command string (NAME=value, export NAME=value) and substitute them before path resolution. (2) If a simple command that is a known reader/egress command, OR any command evaluated while cwd or an assignment references a protected directory, still carries unresolvable $VAR, ${..}, {} or glob tokens after substitution, deny with reason 'dynamic_path_unresolvable' and remediation 'rewrite with a literal path'. (3) New config knob [policy] dynamic_args = deny|warn|allow, default deny. Document that this is the one place veil is fail-closed by design because dynamic args are the canonical bypass.

FALSE POSITIVE BUDGET: run the last 30 days of audit.jsonl (Bash entries) through the new rule offline and report how many historic ALLOWs would flip to DENY; include that number in the bead close comment. Add 'veil replay --audit <path>' as a hidden dev subcommand if useful.

TESTS: assignment substitution, export, multiple assignments, $HOME/$PWD expansion (resolve from hook env), globs inside protected dir (cat data/*.csv already denied - keep), globs outside (allow).
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator at 9dd0d14: full suite 523 passed, 0 failed on a clean export; CI green. Independent probe: find -exec cat {}, ls | xargs cat {}, f=.env; cat $f, echo $(cat .env) all denied (were allowed at 6923d2f). tests/dynamic_args.rs covers xargs/-exec/$var vectors. CI timing guard fixed in the code (min-of-N, 1 ms limit kept; decomposition measured ~1.6x slower, bead records numbers). OPEN OWNER QUESTION, not closed by me: the false-positive rate of denying unresolved words (370 of the replayed denials are programs without a per-command file grammar: aws, sed, curl, jq, cp, cmp) is measured, whether it is acceptable is the owner's call. Not done: cd tracking (bd-vyk), scripts (bd-1bk).

comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
BrownChapel: bd-2mi CHECKPOINT. Pushed to main: 8456a2a (code and tests), aaa22d1 (README). NOT complete, not closing.

## The three probe vectors (HEAD aaa22d1, macOS, scratch HOME, real binary)

| command | repo with `.env` protected by the built-in pack only, no config | repo whose `.veil.toml` lists `.env` |
|---|---|---|
| `f=.env; cat $f` | DENY (resolved to `.env` before judging) | DENY |
| `ls -a \| xargs cat`, `xargs cat {}` | DENY (`dynamic_path_unresolvable`: names read from stdin) | DENY |
| `find . -exec cat {} \;` | ALLOW | DENY |
| `grep -r SECRET .`, `rg SECRET .` | ALLOW | DENY |

The two ALLOWs are the directory walk ignoring built-in packs. That is bd-1si, not the dynamic-argument stance: neither command has an unresolved word. Ignored failing test and output are on bd-1si.

## Acceptance, item by item

1. Track simple assignments and substitute before path resolution: DONE. NAME=value, `export`, multiple assignments, `$HOME`/`~`/`$PWD`, brace lists, quote removal, ANSI-C `$'..'`, and literal `for f in a b; do cat $f; done` (every word judged). A name is trusted only if assigned once; reassigned, `+=`, `read`/`select`/`mapfile`/`getopts`/`printf -v`, `for` with no list, and `$PWD` after `cd` are unknown.
2. Reader/egress command, or any command in a protected context, with an unresolvable `$VAR`, `${..}`, `{}` or glob token is denied as `dynamic_path_unresolvable` with "rewrite with a literal path": DONE for variables, `$( )`, xargs stdin, over-long brace lists and unparsable text. Globs are not "unresolved": they are judged by directory scope as before (`cat data/*.csv` denied, `cat src/*.rs` allowed), which I believe matches the intent; say if it does not. Strict set (denied for any unresolved word, anywhere): known readers (path positions only), content filters, bulk transfers, variable or `$( )` program, unparsable or over-budget text. Everything else: only where cwd or an assignment is protected.
3. `[policy] dynamic_args = deny|warn|allow`, default deny, `VEIL_DYNAMIC_ARGS`, README "Dynamic Arguments" with the fail-closed-by-design statement: DONE. `warn` is audit-only; the agent is not told (README says so).
4. Tests: assignment substitution, export, multiple assignments, `$HOME`/`$PWD`, globs inside a protected directory denied and outside allowed: DONE in tests/dynamic_args.rs (14, real binary, fixtures on disk) plus decomposer and expander unit tests. Mutation-checked: disabling for-loop handling, path-position filtering, assignment tracking, the strict set and the protected-context rule each fail named tests.
5. False-positive budget: MEASURED, see below. Whether the number is acceptable is not mine to declare.

## False-positive budget (the number you asked for)

Replay of the last 30 days, 137 session transcripts, 24,842 distinct (command, cwd) pairs, baseline = HEAD 9b65e08 (24,681 allows):

- first cut: 1,224 of 24,608 allows flipped to deny (4.97%)
- after two refinements (literal `for` loops judged per word; for parsed readers only a word in a file position counts, so `grep "$p" f` and `head -n $n f` pass): **679 of 24,681 (2.75%)**
- of the 681 denials that `dynamic_args = allow` would lift: 672 unresolved argument to a reader, filter or bulk transfer, 5 unanalysable text, 4 a string that assigns a protected path. By shape: 533 variable the command never assigns, 116 `$( )` result, 13 xargs stdin, 14 other.
- by program: aws 168, sed 133, grep 120, rg 36, cat 34, curl 29, jq 15, cp 13, cmp 12. aws, sed, curl, jq, cp and cmp are 370 of them: veil has no per-command grammar for which word is a file, so any unresolved word counts. That is the next lever and is NOT done here.

About 23 commands a day on this machine's history would now be denied. That is the cost; it is not small.

## Not done / remaining for bd-2mi

- per-command parsing for aws, sed, curl, jq, cp, cmp (370 of 681 flips).
- DENY to ALLOW: 3 historic baseline denies are now allowed. Investigation running; result will be a follow-up comment. Until then, treat as unexplained.
- No independent verification. I re-executed my own tests; that is all.

## Disclosures

- Replay uses transcripts as a proxy (audit.jsonl keeps no command text), a scratch HOME with default config (so a user's own protected patterns are absent: protected-context denials are undercounted), and includes this session's own commands (corpus grew 24,608 to 24,842 between runs, so the two percentages have different denominators). It never prints command text.
- A bypass found while probing and fixed with a test: ANSI-C quoting (`cat $'.e\x6ev'`) hid the path; `$'..'` and `$".."` are now decoded.
- Deliberate contract change: the bd-2kr test that pinned variable and unanalysable commands as allowed now asserts deny.
- New, separate bug filed as bd-sve (P1): project `.veil.toml` is read only from the hook cwd, so from a subdirectory `cat ../vault/secret.txt` and even the absolute path are ALLOWED. Reproduced at aaa22d1.
- Known gaps unchanged: `cd` inside a command string not followed (bd-vyk), scripts not read (bd-1bk), macOS only.
- `ubs` on 13 changed files: 30 criticals, none in a runtime path on inspection (28 "secret compared with ==" on byte comparisons in the parser, 2 `panic!` messages in `#[cfg(test)]` helpers). Not independently reviewed.
- The repo pre-commit hook added `.beads/issues.jsonl` to both commits: those are other agents' records (bd-1si, bd-3rn), not my edits.
- Tests run: lib (281, the 4 KiB wall-clock guard fails only under CPU contention from my own replay and passes alone at about 0.5 ms against its 1 ms bound), allowlist, argv_path, bare_invocation, directory_scope, doctor, dynamic_args, golden_rules, operator_manifest, path_decision, protected_corpus, shell_decomposition, spine_denied_flags. rustfmt --check and clippy `-D warnings` clean.
- `crates/boundary-detectors` in the tree is not mine and not part of this bead.

## The 3 historic DENY to ALLOW cases: explained, 2 fixed

Replay of 30 days, baseline HEAD 9b65e08, 3 commands the baseline denied and checkpoint 8456a2a allowed. Command text was masked (quoted strings and long tokens removed) when I looked.

1. `export NAME=<path to a sqlite file>` followed by `npm run ...`: REGRESSION, fixed. The baseline judged the `export` as a command naming the path (a pack-protected database). 8456a2a treated `export` as a pure assignment, so an exported protected path reached the program after it unjudged.
