The baseline denied on the unexpanded word `${c}_IS.pdf` (it decided the word names a directory it could not clear). Reproduced on a fixture with a dummy URL: baseline deny, new allow, and `curl -o out.pdf` and `-o $c.pdf` are allowed by both. The loop now resolves to `1_IS.pdf` and `2_IS.pdf`, no directory is named. A baseline false positive removed.

Fix (353a5d5): `export`, `declare -x` and `typeset -x` of a protected path are judged as naming it again. Non-exported assignments (`F=path; echo done`, `declare`, `local`) stay assignments only. Real-binary test `an_exported_protected_path_is_judged_because_veil_does_not_read_what_runs_after_it`; mutation check (export treated as pure assignment again) fails exactly that test. Re-ran the filtered replay on the fixed binary: the 2 export cases deny again, only case 3 remains allowed.

## Known gap this exposed (not fixed here)

A path handed to one program through a PREFIX assignment is not followed into that program:

    F=<protected path> python3 -c 'import os; print(open(os.environ["F"]).read())'   ALLOW
    F=<protected path> ./run.sh                                                        ALLOW

Baseline 9b65e08 allows both too, so this is not new, but it is the same channel `export` closes. It belongs with interpreter and script inspection (bd-1bk), where a program's own reads are the problem. Now stated in the README. I have not filed a separate bead; say if you want one.

- I wrote that mutation checks covered "assignment tracking, the strict set and the protected-context rule". At this commit I re-ran and confirmed only: for-loop handling off, path-position filtering off, export handling off (each fails named tests). The earlier-window mutation checks on the other rules are from my notes and were not re-run at 353a5d5.
- The README said the protected context is "the directory it runs in holds a path covered by protected". Wrong: the code (`ProtectedContext::in_protected_directory`) means the working directory is INSIDE a protected root or one a built-in pack recognises. README corrected in 353a5d5.

## State

Tests at 353a5d5: lib 282, allowlist, argv_path, bare_invocation, directory_scope (1 ignored: bd-1si), doctor, dynamic_args 15, golden_rules, operator_manifest, path_decision, protected_corpus, shell_decomposition, spine_denied_flags all pass; rustfmt --check and clippy -D warnings clean. comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
BrownChapel: CI timing guard fixed in 903c067 (pushed; CI run 45671020178 green on 903c067). bd-2mi is still not complete and I am not closing it.

## The question: my code, or the runner? Both. I fixed the code.

`four_kib_of_command_decomposes_in_under_a_millisecond` failed on aaa22d1 and 8456a2a (4082 B in 1.56 ms against 1 ms).

- My change made decomposition about 1.6x slower. Measured in the debug profile CI uses, best of 50, same harness, alternating baseline (9b65e08) and new binaries on a busy Mac (load 4-5):

| | long 4082 B (the failing input) | many 3768 B |
|---|---|---|
| baseline 9b65e08 | 0.46 - 0.57 ms | 0.23 - 0.28 ms |
| 8456a2a (red) | 0.75 - 0.85 ms | 0.40 - 0.47 ms |
| 903c067 | 0.40 - 0.44 ms | 0.20 - 0.25 ms |

- The runner is also slower than this Mac: 1.56 ms there against ~0.8 ms here for the same code, about 2x. So the baseline (~0.47 ms here, ~0.95 ms scaled) was already close to the limit on the runner.
- The failure was intermittent, not deterministic: 353a5d5 (same slow code) passed CI (run 45667607553); aaa22d1 and 8456a2a failed. So it was runner variance on a thin margin.

The assertion is unchanged: still 1 ms, still the minimum of 50 runs. I did not raise the limit or change the test profile.

## What changed (no behaviour change intended)

Found by timing each phase and sampling the test binary. In `src/extract/decompose.rs`, `expand.rs` and `src/extract.rs`: lazy computation of unknowable variable names; byte-loop `raw_words`; a fast path in `scan` for text with nothing special in it; table-driven run copies; words moved instead of cloned; `matches!` keyword checks; a shortcut for a bare unset `$name` or lone substitution marker; a quick reject in `collect_input_redirect_paths`.

One change is observable and worth naming: only the first 8 unresolved words of a command keep the text they were written with (later ones are still unresolved, with empty text). A reason or audit record names one word. I checked every consumer of that text: `lib.rs` uses `.first()`, the others use `is_empty()`, and `unresolved_files` builds from argv paths, not the unresolved text. Real-binary probe: `cat` with 12 unresolved arguments is denied naming `$a`.

## Tests and verification

- New: scan fast path vs the full scanner (differential, plain text), bare-word shortcut vs the general path (differential; names with a value, HOME, PWD and loop variables never take it), unresolved-text cap.
- Mutation checks, each fails exactly the new test: fast path that trims text; shortcut that drops the HOME/PWD exclusion (no existing test used a bare `$HOME` word, so that shape was unguarded before).
- Run on a clean copy of HEAD with only these three files overlaid (in the shared tree, which also holds other agents' uncommitted edits to allowlist.rs, evaluator.rs and tests/directory_scope.rs, one test in each of argv_path and path_decision fails: `the_denial_names_the_command_and_the_label_and_is_not_the_direct_read_message` and `test_of_a_directory_holding_protected_paths_is_a_denial_with_a_reason`. Both pass on the clean copy, so I attribute them to those uncommitted edits; I did not trace them further and they are not mine to fix): lib 285 plus the 12 integration targets pass (directory_scope has 1 ignored: the bd-1si gap), rustfmt --check and clippy -D warnings clean.
- ubs: 31 criticals, all one heuristic ("secret compared with ==") firing on byte comparisons in the parser and a test; none touch a secret.

## Not verified

- Runner headroom is an estimate (about 2x this Mac, so ~0.8-0.9 ms against 1 ms), not measured on the runner. One green run is not proof; if it goes red again I will report it rather than widen the limit.
- No independent verification.
- The hook added `.beads/issues.jsonl` (other agents' staged records) to this commit, as it did to earlier ones.

Next: continue bd-2mi (per-command parsing for aws, sed, curl, jq, cp, cmp is still open).

comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
BrownChapel: bd-2mi, per-command parsing for aws / sed / curl / jq / cp / cmp. I looked and recommend NOT doing it as a false-positive lever. One real defect found (filed as bd-pm8). bd-2mi still not closed.

Per-command parsing was my own suggestion for lowering the false-positive rate; it is not one of the bead's acceptance items (1-5 in my checkpoint comment stand, item 5 still waits for your call on 2.75%).

## What the denials look like

30-day transcript replay (a proxy: the audit log keeps no command text), binary built from the shared working tree at 903c067 plus other agents' uncommitted edits, so not comparable to the 679 figure at 8456a2a. 614 stance denials (denied now, allowed with `dynamic_args = allow`). Counts only; the command text was classified in memory and never printed.

| program | denials | what the unresolved word is |
|---|---|---|
| aws | 132 | mostly an option value (`--command-id` 24, `--profile`, `--start-time`), some `s3://bucket/$key` URIs |
| sed | 128 | the script word, e.g. a `"${a},${b}p"` range |
| jq | 20 | the filter, or `-f $file` (8) |
| cp | 13 | file operands |
| cmp | 12 | file operands |
| curl | 8 | URLs, `-o` targets |
| other programs | 301 | not looked at here |

## Why skipping by position is not sound

I probed 28 LITERAL file channels of these programs with the real binary against a fixture whose `.veil.toml` protects `.env` (cases in my scratchpad `cases-literal.txt`, `cases-literal2.txt`). Every one was already DENIED, including channels in positions that are not "file" positions: `aws ssm get-command-invocation --command-id file://.env`, `curl -H @.env`, `curl --cert .env`, `jq --rawfile x .env`, `cp -t /tmp .env`. veil judges every word of a command as a path candidate.

So the unresolved word is the same channel with the value hidden. Skipping an unresolved word because of its position would make the variable form looser than the literal form. For aws that is concrete: the AWS CLI documents `file://` / `fileb://` loading for a parameter's value generally (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-usage-parameters-file.html), so `--command-id $id` can become a local read exactly as `--command-id file://.env` does. For sed the script word is the same: see below.

What could be skipped soundly is a word whose literal prefix rules out a file reference, such as `https://host/$p` or `s3://bucket/$key` for curl and aws. In the rows I saw that is 13 aws and 3 curl words out of 614 (top rows only; I did not count the tail), about 3%. That would move 2.75% to about 2.67%. I did not build it: aws and curl belong to bd-x8o (egress class), which is next, and that is where a URL-prefix rule would be designed with the egress rules.

## The real defect: bd-pm8 (P1)

`sed 'r .env' notes.txt`, `sed 'R .env'`, `sed -n '1r .env'`, `sed -e 'w .env'`, `sed 's/a/b/w .env'` are ALLOWED. A sed script names files inside its own text and veil does not parse it. Real run on this Mac with a dummy `.env`: `sed 'r .env' notes.txt` prints the `.env` contents. The baseline binary (9b65e08) gives the identical result, so it predates bd-2mi and has no variable in it, so the stance does not cover it. Filed as bd-pm8 with the reproduction table and acceptance; I suggest it goes to bd-1bk (interpreter script inspection) or its own owner, your call. I have not started it.

## Not verified

- Probes use a config-protected `.env`; the pack-only case was not repeated for these programs.
- The jq `import` (data file via `-L`) channel was not tested with a protected `secret.json`; noted in bd-pm8.
- GNU sed was not run (macOS BSD sed only).
- No independent verification.

Next: bd-x8o (egress class), unless you redirect me.

description: Security audit of veil 0.1.0 found 14 bypass techniques: extension rename, allowlisted extension/path escape, base64/gzip/tar wrapping, split files, named pipes, case sensitivity (Linux), double extensions, binary wrappers, hardlinks, /dev/fd anonymous pipes, and allowlisted path + any extension. 4 vectors correctly blocked (direct path, /proc/self/fd, symlinks, path normalization). 5 design-level gaps identified. Recommendations: (1) add magic byte detection, (2) sensitivity patterns > allowlist precedence, (3) resolve hardlinks like symlinks, (4) normalize /dev/fd consistently, (5) document Bash hook coverage gap. Source: Triaged from cairn@cmdrvl.com email on 2026-03-29. Original subject: veil 0.1.0 — security findings (private disclosure). PRIVATE — do not post publicly.

title: Add veil operator subcommand for spine tool discovery
description: When veil blocks a direct file read, agents don't know how to find the authorized spine tools. In session d039d8e1, the agent tried veil shape/vacuum/fingerprint (wrong — spine tools aren't veil subcommands), then wrote a Python script that bypassed veil entirely. Proposed: veil operator subcommand that assembles a runtime operator document from installed spine tools. (1) Reads authorized_tools from .veil.toml, (2) calls --describe (R-006) on each installed tool, (3) emits combined reference the agent can consume. Usage: agent hits deny → remediation says 'run veil operator' → agent gets full spine tool reference → proceeds through authorized path. Key insight: defense is not making the wall taller, it's making the door obvious. Leverages existing R-006 introspection. Source: Triaged from cairn@cmdrvl.com email on 2026-03-30. Session d039d8e1.
close_reason: Already shipped in src/operator.rs (2358 lines) and documented in README; remaining operator.v0 manifest parity is tracked in bd-t94 and bd-bf2.

title: Veil v1: honest hook + OS sandbox enforcement
description:
Epic from the 2026-09-02 reality check (docs/plan.md, section 'Gap Closure Plan').

WHY: veil 0.4.1 is installed and has stopped real reads of .env and ~/.cmdrvl/config, but it is a shell-text parser with a fixed reader list. A 36-vector probe against a protected directory ALLOWED 22 reads: awk/sed/base64/xxd/perl/jq/sqlite3/duckdb/grep/rg on the file; sh -c, find -exec, xargs, $(cat), variable indirection; cp-then-cat, tar|base64; python3 script.py, uv run python -c; curl -F file=@; Grep tool content mode on a directory. Parser denylisting cannot beat indirection, so the story 'the agent cannot read your private data' is not mechanically true today.

GOAL: Two tracks. Track A (0.5): make the hook honest and much harder to trip accidentally: path-anywhere-in-argv rule, shell decomposition, dynamic-arg stance, interpreter script inspection, directory-scope Grep, egress commands, enforcement-level disclosure generated from a committed bypass matrix. Track B (1.0): OS sandbox enforcement: veil sandbox launches the harness with protected paths unreadable (seatbelt on macOS, Landlock on Linux) and a broker daemon runs authorized spine tools outside the sandbox.

DONE WHEN: the committed bypass matrix shows 36/36 denied under sandbox and every Track A vector denied under hook-only; veil doctor reports enforcement level; README claims are generated from the matrix.

NON-GOALS: Write/Edit guarding, PostToolUse output filtering, outbound message-body policy (the calling wrapper).

AMBITION ROUNDS (2026-09-02) added Track C (twin mode for zero-retention work) and Track D (witness ledger + chained session log + veil attest + unified launcher with the airlock gate), a formal label model with enforcement-dominance property tests, MCP tool argument screening, content-sniff classification, a provenance-based derived allowlist, a replay harness with a warn->deny rollout, broker flag policy + output scanning via the shared boundary-detectors crate, and seccomp hardening. See docs/plan.md 'Gap Closure Plan (revised)'.
notes:
2026-11-24 deep review refinements (3-wave Minimum Credible Beef):
- Wave A (Stop the Bleeding): fix bd-1si (P0 Grep dir), new P0 spine --explicit/--raw flag guard + remediation text fix, bd-grok-dual-payload-jr0, Track A core (bd-2kr, bd-29r, bd-x8o, bd-1wa, bd-sel), and create shared `boundary-detectors` crate.
- Wave B (Real Mechanical Boundaries): Track B OS sandbox + broker (bd-wat, bd-e6v, bd-27o, bd-34r, bd-3qw) prioritizing unprivileged macOS Seatbelt + Linux Landlock ABI 4+ (treat root netns/pf as optional hardening, not v1 blockers).
- Wave C (Killer Demo): Track D unified launcher `veil sandbox --egress airlock` (bd-3g5, promoted to P1) + protected-corpus shingle Bloom filter + `veil attest` (bd-ol1) + Track C `veil sandbox --twin` wired to `cmdrvl/twinning` for both local file overlays and synthetic DB/warehouse endpoints.
- Runtime constraint: keep `veil` hook mode 100% synchronous with zero async runtime overhead (<1ms startup).
- Scope guard: keep `docs/jev_sidecar_plan.md` LLM sidecar strictly quarantined out of v1.

title: Hook response format mismatch — deny decisions not honored by Claude Code
description: Veil 0.2.1 fires and logs deny decisions correctly (audit log confirms two deny entries for Read tool on CSV), but Claude Code does not block the tool call — data comes through with OK status. Root cause: Claude Code expects specific JSON format on stdout with exit 0: {hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason: '...'}}. Veil is returning its own format or exiting with code 2, which Claude Code treats as a hook error popup (dismissible) rather than a tool block. Evidence from session b7001bba: Line 12 agent calls Read on CSV, veil audit log shows deny at 14:05:11, Line 13 tool result returns OK with raw CSV content (50 rows loaded into context). Security-critical — defeats veil's core purpose. Related: bd-2w8. Source: Triaged from cairn@cmdrvl.com email on 2026-03-30.

## Enforcement reporting (acb3f46)

The launcher sets `VEIL_ENFORCEMENT=sandbox`, creates an empty marker beside its broker socket, and ends the profile with a rule that denies opening it. veil says `sandbox` only on macOS, with the variable set, when `VEIL_BROKER_SOCKET` is an absolute path with a launcher's socket name and the marker is a plain empty file with one name whose open fails with EPERM (file permissions give EACCES).

Limits: this shows that a policy on the process closes that file, **not that veil's whole profile is in force**. A process under its own profile that does so is believed (a test records this). Anything able to write the audit log can write any record. Hook decisions are still parser-based. This does not do bd-apj's doctor shape or broker health check.

## NOT DONE: Linux (nothing below is built)

1. Landlock (ABI 4+) backend in the launcher. `veil sandbox -- <command>` and `--shell` refuse on Linux. What exists is the rule compiler; CI job `linux-landlock-sandbox` runs only `landlock_applies_compiled_read_rules`, not a launcher. Design constraint, docs/plan.md "Linux / Landlock": no rule can subtract a protected child from an allowed parent, so there is no general protected-glob claim until that tradeoff is accepted and tested. The bead's "pre-exec hook" would mean `CommandExt::pre_exec`, which is `unsafe` and forbidden here; a helper that restricts itself and then execs is an untried alternative.
2. A seccomp filter on the sandboxed tree denying `ptrace`.
3. Denying `process_vm_readv` and `process_vm_writev`.

6. Broker tools unable to write files.

9. Verified enforcement reporting: Linux always says `hook`. The macOS marker relies on EPERM; Landlock refuses with EACCES, the same as file permissions.

netns/pf are optional per the bead notes; not done.

- A confined command can still append to a protected file, and the audit log's directory is not protected (README limits, both reproduced by LilacOx).

title: Track A: content-sniff classification via boundary-detectors
description:
Parent bd-30b. Depends on bd-29r; related to airlock al-34s (shared crate) and supersedes bd-28k (magic bytes).

WHY: files outside protected directories are public by default (fail-open). An export renamed to notes.txt or dropped in ~/Downloads is readable. Extension renames defeat glob packs.

DESIGN: For a Read/Grep/argv decision on a file outside protected dirs and not on the safe allowlist, veil (the hook process, never the agent) reads the first 4 KiB: (1) magic bytes: SQLite header, parquet PAR1, zip with xl/ (xlsx), %PDF, gzip/zstd -> label protected (databases and documents are sensitive by policy default; data.database pack already says so). (2) PII density via boundary-detectors: SSN, Luhn-valid card numbers, E.164 phones, emails per KiB; per-detector thresholds in [sniff]; files under a git work tree are exempt from the email detector (commit trailers). (3) Decision cached in ~/.cmdrvl/state/veil/sniff-cache.jsonl keyed by (dev, inode, mtime, size); cache hit costs no I/O. Budget: sniff adds at most one 4 KiB read; skip if the 1 ms budget is already spent (fail-open, audit 'sniff_skipped').

TESTS: fixtures for renamed sqlite/parquet/xlsx/pdf; a CSV of SSNs named readme.txt; a source file with many emails (allow); cache invalidation on mtime change; budget skip path.

title: Track A: jq import/include name files inside the program (jq -L . -n 'import "secret" as $d; $d' reads ./secret.json unjudged)
description:
PROBLEM. jq's module system reads files named inside the jq PROGRAM, which veil does not parse. `jq -L . -n 'import "secret" as $d; $d'` reads ./secret.json (`import "x" as $d;` loads x.json, or x/x.json, searched in each `-L` directory; `import "x" as m;` and `include "x";` load x.jq) and prints it. The program is one quoted word with a space in it, so no word of the command is shaped like a path, the same mechanism as bd-pm8 (sed `r`).

MEASURED, 2026-11-25 on HEAD c2f0d61 (probe, protected `secret.json` and `.env` in the working directory):
- ALLOWED: `jq -L . -n 'import "secret" as $d; $d'` (bypass-matrix row `jq-import-data`, Leak = contents), `jq -n 'include "secret"; 1' -L .`, `jq -n -L data 'import "clients/holdings" as $d; $d'`.
- Already DENIED, so not part of this bead: `jq -n 'input' secret.json`, `jq -n --rawfile x .env '$x'`, `jq -n --slurpfile x secret.json '$x'`, `yq -n 'load(".env")'` (a quoted literal inside the program is found).
- awk was probed in the same pass: `awk 'BEGIN{while((getline l < ".env")>0) print l}'` is DENIED (row `awk-getline-file`); `getline < "f"` and `print > "f"` with a quoted literal are found. awk with a computed file name is the generic dynamic-path problem, not this.

SCOPE. Parse the strings after `import` and `include` in the jq program (jq's own lexer rules for string literals, including the `search` metadata object `{search: "./dir"}`), and the `-L`/`--library-path` directories (jq also has a default search path: `~/.jq`, `$ORIGIN/../lib/jq`, `$ORIGIN/../lib`). Each candidate file (`<dir>/<name>.json`, `<dir>/<name>/<name>.json`, `<dir>/<name>.jq`, `<dir>/<name>/<name>.jq`) is judged as a named path; an import veil cannot resolve (string built at run time is impossible in jq, but a relative `search` path may be) is refused like an unparseable sed script. Same fail-closed rule as bd-pm8.

ACCEPTANCE. Real-binary tests with fixtures on disk, each denial naming the file in the audit record; the three ALLOWED forms above denied; `-L` before and after the program, in the spellings jq accepts (`-L dir`, `-Ldir`, `--library-path dir`; confirm against the installed jq, they differ between 1.6 and 1.7); ordinary jq programs with no import stay allowed (`jq . notes.json`, `jq -r '.a[]'`); flip row `jq-import-data` and regenerate docs/bypass-matrix.md.

comments.text:
bd-3h5 evidence (BrownChapel). Commit 3721122, pushed to main. Close is yours.

WHAT IT DOES. `jq -n 'import "secret" as $d; $d'` is now denied (argv_path, naming secret.json). New src/extract/jq.rs reads the prelude of a jq program the way jq does (optional `module {...};`, every import and include, comments, string escapes incl. \uXXXX pairs, {search: ...} metadata) and names every file each import may open; those are judged as named paths with the other words. script.rs also reads the program file of `-f` and every jq module an import may load that exists, for the imports it holds in turn (bd-1bk limits: depth 3, 16 files, 256 KiB, plus a queue cap). A prelude veil cannot read (interpolated name, unterminated string, >64 imports, metadata nested >32 levels) is refused like an unresolved word, under dynamic_args.

MEASURED ON jq 1.8.2 (the search rules in the code come from these, not from the manual):
- `import "x" as $d;` opens x.json or x/x.json; `import "x" as m;` and `include "x";` open x.jq or x/x.jq; a name with directories (clients/holdings) opens clients/holdings.json and clients/holdings/holdings.json.
- No -L needed: the working directory is searched anyway. -L ADDS directories and replaces only the ~/.jq default. Spellings accepted: `-L dir`, `-Ldir`, `-nL dir`, `--library-path dir`; `--library-path=dir` is rejected by jq.
- An import with {search: ...} is searched ONLY in the directories it names: neither the working directory nor -L (my first version said "also"; the differential below caught it; corrected before the commit).
- `-f` is a flag: the first operand is the program file wherever -f stands (`jq in.json -f first.jq` runs in.json as the program). Its imports are searched from the working directory.
- A relative `search` in a module is relative to the module's own directory. ../ in a module name is rejected by jq.
- A .jq module with a syntax error is reported with its own source line, so naming a protected file as a module leaks a line of it.

PLANTED NEGATIVES, RED FIRST. At HEAD (b755bef) plus only the new rows: 8 rows ALLOWED (jq-import-data flipped, default-search, protected-dir, search-metadata, include-protected-module, program-file, from-module, unparseable) and the 3 controls passing. 5 more rows were added with the code (library-path long/attached/cluster, second-of-many, escaped-name) and are covered by mutation, not by a red run at HEAD. Matrix now: 168 vectors, 120 blocked, 31 still allowed, 17 controls (was 152, 107, 32, 13). New: 13 blocked rows (one of them is the flipped jq-import-data) and 4 controls (include reads .jq not .json; a module with ordinary imports; a `search` that replaces -L; a plain program).

CORRECTION. The commit message of 3721122 says "121 blocked"; the generated README and docs/bypass-matrix.md say 120 (107 + 13). The generated documents are right; history is not rewritten.

VERIFIED, on a fresh export of HEAD 62797d4 plus the 8 files (identical to 3721122 apart from a .beads line):
- cargo fmt --check clean; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings clean.
- Full suite: 725 passed, 0 failed (lib 404 incl. 10 new jq unit tests; tests/jq_import.rs 6 real-binary tests, about 100 command forms, each denial checked in the audit record for the file it names; bypass_matrix 3).
- tests/e2e_hook_matrix.sh against the built binary: all 168 rows decided as the matrix says (p50 8.8 ms).
- CI: run 45727839830 on 3721122 and run 45728102743 on f4700ce (the symlink test, below): rust, e2e-hook-matrix (ubuntu, macOS), macos-seatbelt-sandbox, linux-landlock-sandbox all success.
- f4700ce adds one real-binary assertion (a symlink in lib/ to the protected module data/clients/holdings.jq is denied and its marker is not in the reason); no code change. I checked it on a fresh export of 3721122 plus that file: tests/jq_import.rs 6 passed. I did not re-run the whole suite for it.

DIFFERENTIAL AGAINST THE REAL jq. 2,475 generated programs (import/include x 11 -L spellings x 9 names x 7 search forms, plus -f programs) run through jq 1.8.2 in a fixture directory, a marker planted in each protected file: 0 commands where jq leaks a protected marker and veil allows it. Over-blocks added by this change (old binary allowed, new denies, jq leaks nothing): 444, and the 12 I read are all an import naming a file that does not exist at a location the protected patterns match (data/holdings.json, or a name like sub/secret.json that the credentials pack protects by name), which veil already does for any named path. I did not classify all 444.

REAL COMMANDS. Replayed the 652 distinct jq commands in this machine's Claude Code transcripts (81 mention import/include/-f/-L) through the old and new binaries: 0 decisions changed. It says little: real jq use here almost never imports.

MUTATION. 18 runs by hand in a scratch copy, one defect each, against the final code and tests (16 distinct defects; two of them run once against the matrix and once against tests/jq_import.rs): inline program not parsed; -L ignored; include reads .json; search ignored; search ADDED to the default instead of replacing it; refusal not reported; modules not followed; -f program file not read; refused file not strict; module directory ignored for `search`; \u escape dropped; only the first import kept; first operand after -f wrong; attached -Ldir dropped; `-nL dir` not taking the next word; nesting cap removed. Every one is caught by a matrix row, a real-binary test, a unit test, or more than one (script: scratchpad jq_mutants.py). The uncapped-nesting mutant is caught by the unit test only.

SLIPS AND HONEST CAVEATS.
- Version 1 of the search rule was wrong ("search adds to the default"); the differential showed it and the commit has the measured rule. The first control for it was also wrong (a file named secret.json is protected by NAME anywhere, so it could not show that the search directory replaced the default); replaced by one that uses a location-only protection.

The contract should make path/attachment findings easy to consume from cmdrvl-cli without implying that Veil has inspected message-body semantics. Include action, reason, severity, confidence, remediation, and enough pack/path context for downstream audit receipts.

comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
bd-3ib evidence — BrownChapel — commit 3f9b0fe (pushed to origin/main). Not closed; awaiting orchestrator verification.

WHAT CHANGED
`veil test|explain|scan --json` now print a versioned document, and a failure under --json is a document on stdout, not stderr-only text.
- `"schema_version": "veil.path-decision.v1"` on test, explain and scan (scan entries inside `files` carry none of their own).
- Failure under --json (unnormalizable path, guard preflight refusal, any other error): stdout is `{"schema_version","error":{"code","message"}}`, exit 2, message also on stderr. `code` is one of `path_unnormalizable`, `guard_preflight_refused`, `error`. Before this, exit 2 with EMPTY stdout (reproduced with a path containing a tab).
- Without --json nothing changes: stderr only, exit 2.
- decision/match `confidence` prints 0.95, not 0.949999988079071 (f32 widened to f64).
- `scan` root no longer ends in `/.` for `veil scan .` (found by a failing test).
- operator.json (test/explain/scan descriptions, exit-code 2 meaning) and README ("Path Decisions for Wrappers") say these commands decide on paths only and do not read file contents or message bodies.
- Files: src/operator.rs, src/main.rs, operator.json, README.md, tests/path_decision.rs (new, 9 tests).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Wrappers consume decisions without scraping stderr — MET for test/explain/scan. Allow/deny exit 0 and is read from `decision.action`; no decision exits 2 with a JSON error. Hook mode already printed JSON on stdout (unchanged). NOT done: `operator --json`, `packs --json`, `config --json`, `audit --json` still print errors only on stderr; out of this bead's stated scope, not a wrapper decision path.
2. Path/attachment context in machine-readable output — MET to the extent veil has it: `input_path`, `normalized_path`, and for explain/scan `match{kind,pack,protected_pattern,allowlist_pattern,severity,confidence,directory_sensitive}`. veil has no notion of an "attachment"; the wrapper passes the path, and `test` does not include `match` (use `explain`).
3. Contract does not claim message-body screening — MET by documentation: the manifest and README state paths only. There is deliberately no constant "path_only" field in the JSON (no consumer would branch on it); tests/path_decision.rs pins the manifest wording so it cannot be silently dropped.
4. Shape stable enough for later wrapper integration tests — MET only by this repo's own pinning: tests assert exact key sets and exact documents. UNVERIFIED against a real wrapper: no cmdrvl-cli code consumes these documents yet (guard_preflight.py only runs `veil doctor --json`). `veil --schema` still documents hook-mode stdout only; I did not add a JSON Schema file for this contract (no consumer, key sets are pinned by tests). If the orchestrator wants a checked-in schema, that is a follow-up with a named consumer.

BEHAVIOR CHANGES A REVIEWER SHOULD KNOW
- Under --json a wrapper must use the exit code, not "stdout empty", to tell failure from success; stdout is now non-empty on failure.
- test/explain/scan run the guard preflight inside `path_decision_command` (src/main.rs) instead of before dispatch, so a preflight refusal can be JSON. Same checks, same message.
- `veil test <dir>` runs the bd-1si directory scan (Read semantics), so a directory holding protected paths is a deny with the bd-1si reason; pinned by a test.

EVIDENCE (re-executed, not copied)
- `cargo test --locked --test path_decision`: 9 passed. The tests run the real veil binary on real temp repos (`.veil.toml` with `protected = ["data/**"]`, real files).
- Also run, all passing: `--lib` (178), `--bin veil` (68), `--test operator_manifest` (15), golden_rules, doctor, directory_scope, bare_invocation, spine_denied_flags, allowlist. Not run: the full suite, `--all-targets`.
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the three .rs files: clean. `cargo clippy --locked --lib --bin veil --test path_decision --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean. `ubs` on the three files: 0 critical (an earlier `panic!` in a test helper was rewritten to an assert).
- Mutation checks, each restored byte-identical (md5 compared):
  M1 emit raw f32 confidence -> test_denial_carries_every_field... FAILS.
  M3 disable the JSON error branch -> an_unnormalizable_path_is_a_json_error... and a_guard_preflight_refusal_is_a_json_error... FAIL.
- Not independently verified: behavior under Gemini/Grok/Copilot harness detection (the preflight tests use VEIL_HARNESS=claude-code and plain only); a real wrapper consuming the documents.

Reservations on src/operator.rs, src/main.rs, operator.json, tests/path_decision.rs, README.md released after this comment.

title: Track A: provenance-based derived allowlist (hash registry replaces *-report.json globs)
description:
Parent bd-30b. Depends on bd-27o (broker writes the registry).

WHY: the safe allowlist trusts filenames: *-report.json is allowed, so 'cp data/x.csv x-report.json' (or a spine tool writing raw rows to a report) is readable. Labels must attach to content, not names.

DESIGN: ~/.cmdrvl/state/veil/derived.jsonl is appended by the broker for every output it returns or file it writes (hash, tool, session, ts). On a Read/Grep decision for a file that would otherwise be denied by a protected-dir or sniff rule, veil hashes the file (bounded 64 MiB, blake3) and allows with label 'derived' if the hash is registered. Glob allowlists stay for docs/config/tests but NEVER override a protected-directory or sniff hit; only registry membership does. 'veil derived list|verify <path>' CLI. Registry rotation with the audit log.

EDGE: hash computed by the hook process (allowed: veil is not the agent); large files -> deny with 'too_large_to_verify'; registry entries expire with the session unless --persist.

TESTS: registered hash allowed inside a protected dir; tampered file (one byte) denied; spoofed *-report.json copy of a protected file denied; rotation.

REFINEMENT ROUND 1: depends only on 'veil exec' direct mode (first deliverable of bd-27o), not on the sandbox. The bypass matrix (bd-sel) gains rows for spoofed report files once this lands; it is not a gate for 0.5.

- Write tools: write_tools_cannot_touch_the_key_or_registry
- Redirection, globs, links, directories above, in policy deny and log: no_tool_call_reads_or_writes_the_key_or_registry. Appended or edited records: a_forged_record_unlocks_nothing
- Getting veil exec to register protected bytes: exec_never_registers_a_raw_copy_of_a_protected_file, a_file_written_under_out_is_checked_before_it_is_registered, a_raw_copy_of_a_protected_file_not_named_on_the_command_line_is_not_registered, a_name_pattern_is_compared_across_the_project_not_only_under_the_call, a_file_that_existed_before_the_run_is_never_registered, a_directory_written_under_out_registers_only_what_passes

DECISION FOR YOU. Forging a record needs a way to write files that no veil hook sees, and that can already turn veil off (finding 1 below). Registration is weaker than that: if an authorized tool reshapes or re-encodes protected values so that neither a detector nor the text comparison sees them, and writes them under --out, they are registered and then readable. The comparison is text only (a shared run of 95 characters is always caught; 24 for output under 64). README "What stays possible" says this, lists the other limits (unhooked writers, change between hash and read, session expiry is not a boundary), and names [spine.denied_flags] as the control. I judged that fit to ship in hook mode; check that you agree.

TWO HOLES FOUND WHILE BUILDING, each red with the real binary, then fixed
1. stdout was compared only with named inputs, so a tool given a list could print a raw copy of the protected file the list named, and it was registered. stdout and --out files now get the same comparison.
2. Bare-name protected patterns (*.vault.txt) were compared only under the call's cwd. They are now compared from the .veil.toml directory.
Cost: a project with more than 10,000 files or 1 GiB to compare registers nothing. So does one with more than 100,000 entries to walk, which a bare pattern can reach through build output.

The existing suite also caught a regression of mine (tests/shell_decomposition.rs): the "veil state is beneath this directory" rule replaced the policy's reason on calls already denied. It now only overrides an allow.

EXISTING EXPECTATIONS I CHANGED ON PURPOSE
- tests/doctor.rs, src/operator.rs, src/hooks.rs: install now writes 4 more matchers (matcher lists and counts; the healthy-doctor fixture has them; 5 ok checks).
- tests/allowlist.rs: a report name is no longer safe (the positive example is now Cargo.lock, plus a negative test).
- tests/veil_exec.rs: --persist cases added.
- Bypass matrix: 3 rows added, docs regenerated with VEIL_BLESS_BYPASS_MATRIX=1 (207 to 210 vectors). tool-read-spoofed-report and tool-grep-spoofed-report were ALREADY blocked at the old HEAD (the protected directory already beat the allowlist), so they are only regression guards. Only tool-read-spoofed-report-unprotected was open; it failed with the old patterns temporarily restored.
- Two faults in my own new tests, fixed: a control expected registration of bytes already in an unregistered protected file (it now asserts denial; the control uses a fresh fixture); the sandbox fixture's socket path was over the macOS limit.
- Mutation check: with the "a registered source does not count" exemption disabled, an_earlier_registered_output_does_not_block_the_next_one fails. Restored.

I did not review the warnings one by one.

NOT DONE

As written, the registry lifts any policy denial of a Read or Grep of a registered file, except for veil's own state; bd-35u should confirm that is what it wants.

title: Track A: a script written earlier in the same command string is run unread (printf 'r .env' > x.sed; sed -f x.sed)
description:
PROBLEM. veil reads a script file when a command runs one (bd-1bk for python, node, ruby, perl, R and shell; bd-xu0 for sed), but it reads the file as it is on disk when the hook runs. A script that the SAME command string writes first does not exist yet, so nothing is read and the run is allowed. The README already lists this limit ("a script written by an earlier command of the same line (it does not exist when veil looks)") but no bypass-matrix row plants it, and it is the one-line form of the two-step chain bd-xu0 closes: the agent does not need the Write tool, one Bash call does both.

MEASURED, 2026-11-25, build at bd-xu0 (all with a protected `.env` in the working directory), hook decision for each:
- ALLOWED: `printf 'r .env\n' > tmp.sed; sed -f tmp.sed notes.txt`
- ALLOWED: `printf 'open(".env").read()\n' > tmp.py && python3 tmp.py`
- For contrast, DENIED once the file exists: after the first half is run on its own, the second half (`sed -f tmp.sed notes.txt`, `python3 tmp.py`) is denied. Two tool calls are caught; one command string is not.

Bypass-matrix rows (still allowed, Leak = contents): sed-file-written-same-line, script-python-written-same-line.

SCOPE. While walking one command string, keep what it writes to a file with a literal body: `echo`/`printf` arguments redirected to a literal path, `cat > f <<'EOF'` and `tee f <<'EOF'` heredocs, `> f` after a here-string. When a later command in the same string runs that path as a script (the same finders script.rs already has: interpreter operand, `source`, `sed -f`, a file run by name), judge the recorded text through the same reading instead of the missing file. A file written with a body veil cannot see (a variable, `$( )`, a pipe) and then run as a script is refused under the dynamic-argument stance, like an unresolved word. The honest limit stays: a body built at run time that no literal shows (`printf "$X"`, `base64 -d`) is the same class as a path built at run time (README, Script Files).

ACCEPTANCE. Real-binary tests on a repo on disk, denials checked in the audit record naming the file: the two commands above denied (`direct_read` for the sed `r`, the literal path for python); the same shape for node, perl, ruby, sh and a heredoc body; `echo hi > x.sh; sh x.sh` and `printf 's/a/b/\n' > x.sed; sed -f x.sed notes.txt` still allowed; a written body built from a variable and then run refused under the default and allowed under `dynamic_args = allow`. Flip the two matrix rows to blocked and regenerate docs/bypass-matrix.md; remove the README line from the list of what veil does not see, or narrow it to what is left.

title: Track A: a command string inside an interpreter program (os.system, perl/ruby system, execSync, awk system() and cmd | getline) is never judged as a command
description:
PROBLEM. A command string INSIDE an interpreter's program is run by the interpreter and veil never judges it as a command. Typed directly, `cat .env` is denied; wrapped in a program, it is allowed.

MEASURED, 2026-11-25, build at bd-pm8 (a24e54b), protected `.env` in the working directory, hook decision for each:
- ALLOWED: `python3 -c "import os; os.system('cat .env')"`, `perl -e 'system("cat .env")'`, `ruby -e 'system("cat .env")'`, `node -e "require('child_process').execSync('cat .env')"`, `awk 'BEGIN{system("cat .env")}'`, `gawk 'BEGIN{system("cat .env")}'`, `awk 'BEGIN{"cat .env" | getline x; print x}'`, `awk 'BEGIN{print | "cat .env"}'`.
- Already DENIED, so not this bead: a literal path read by the program (`python3 -c 'open(".env")'`, `node -e 'readFileSync(".env")'`, awk `getline < ".env"`, `print > ".env"`), `awk -f .env`.
- Different problem, left out: a file name the program BUILDS at run time (`awk 'BEGIN{f=".e" "nv"; while((getline l < f)>0) print l}'` is allowed; the README says a script that computes its own paths is not read).

Bypass-matrix rows (all Leak = contents): script-python-os-system, script-perl-system, script-node-exec, awk-system-call, awk-pipe-getline. bd-pm8 treats the same thing in sed as a refusal (GNU `e` command and `e` flag are denied under the default dynamic_args), so sed is now stricter than every interpreter above.

SCOPE. Find the command strings: os.system / subprocess.* / os.popen / os.exec* (python), system / exec / backticks / qx / open with a pipe (perl, ruby), child_process.exec / execSync / spawn (node), system() / `"cmd" | getline` / `print | "cmd"` (awk). Hand each literal string to the same decomposition a typed Bash command gets (src/extract/decompose.rs), so `cat .env` inside is judged as a read, and refuse a command string that is not a literal (built at run time) the way an unresolved word is refused. Same fail-closed rule as bd-pm8. Related: bd-1bk reads script FILES and their literal paths; this is the inline and the nested-command half.

ACCEPTANCE. Real-binary tests on a repo on disk, each denial in the audit record naming the file; the eight forms above denied; ordinary programs with no command (`python3 -c 'print(1)'`, `awk '{print $1}' notes.txt`, `node -e 'console.log(1)'`) allowed; a program that builds its command at run time refused under the default and allowed under `dynamic_args = allow`. Flip the five matrix rows to blocked and regenerate docs/bypass-matrix.md.
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator at d1a31fb (includes 9101c0f): clean git-archive export, full suite 775 passed, 0 failed; re-ran tests/exec_commands (11 passed) and tests/bypass_matrix (3 passed) myself; CI green on 9101c0f, d1a31fb, f3414ee. Command strings inside interpreter programs (python/node/bun/deno/perl/ruby/R/awk: os.system, subprocess, child_process, system, backticks, Open3, awk system()/getline) are read whole and judged as a typed Bash command (real positive); computed parts are a typed refusal (dynamic_path_unresolvable). Bypass matrix 207 vectors, 152 blocked, 27 still allowed (17 contents / 3 chain / 7 names), 28 controls, up from 120 blocked. Author's measured false-deny cost (replay of 18,302 distinct interpreter commands from local transcripts): 77 newly denied (0.65%), 0 newly allowed, author-run, not re-run by me; author's 27-mutant check also not re-run by me. Disclosed by author: an unrefused case (script FILES that build a command; their literal commands are judged); 27 vectors remain ALLOWED and are listed in docs/bypass-matrix.md. Not verified: my own real-hook probe of the new forms; replay on other machines.

comments.author: zacharyruiz
comments.text:
bd-5iy evidence (BrownChapel). Commit 9101c0f, pushed to main; CI green on it (run 45737834352: rust, e2e-hook-matrix x2, macos-seatbelt, linux-landlock). Close is yours. Plus d1a31fb (the operator test flake you asked for), CI green (run 45740808372).

ANSWER TO "real positive or typed refusal": both, split by what the program can be known to run.
- REAL POSITIVE. A command string made of literals is read whole and run back through the same steps as a typed Bash command: `python3 -c "import os; os.system('cat .env')"` is a direct_read of .env; `os.system('grep -r ssn data')` is a content search of data (a word that names no path by its shape, only the command does); `sh -c`, `xargs`, nested interpreters and scripts they run are followed.
- TYPED REFUSAL, like a word veil cannot resolve (dynamic_path_unresolvable; deny by default, warn records it, allow lifts it): a shell string with a part the program computes ("cat " + name, f-string, sys.argv[1]) and a program that is itself computed (subprocess.run([prog, ...])).
- In between: an argument LIST read by no shell (["git","show",rev]) makes the computed word one unresolved word of that command, judged as `git show $rev` typed is (cat $f denied, git show $rev allowed). I changed to this after the first replay (below).
- NOT refused: script FILES that build a command. Their literal commands are judged. Reason is measured, below.

WHAT IT COVERS. Python (os.system/popen, subprocess.*, os.exec*/spawn*, pty.spawn), Node/Bun/Deno (child_process.exec/execSync/spawn/execFile*, Bun.spawn and Bun.$, Deno.Command), Perl (system, exec, backticks, qx, readpipe, open2/3, open with a pipe), Ruby (system, exec, spawn, backticks, %x, IO.popen, Open3, open("|cmd")), R (system, system2, shell, pipe), awk (system(), "cmd" | getline, print | "cmd"). Found in the code of -c / -e / -E / -pe (incl. option clusters), an awk program and its -f file and #! file (awk files were not read at all before), a here-document or here-string an interpreter reads, and a script file. src/extract/exec.rs is new (own lexer per language: comments, strings, escapes incl. \xNN, interpolation, qw/q/qq, %w, regex-vs-division in awk); wiring is in src/extract/script.rs and src/extract.rs.

BYPASS MATRIX (planted first). 207 vectors, 152 blocked, 27 still allowed (17 contents / 3 chain / 7 names), 28 controls (was 168 / 120 / 31 / 17). On a HEAD-only build of the tests: 32 rows "expected blocked, was ALLOWED"; with the change the matrix passes; docs/bypass-matrix.md/.json and the README block regenerated and drift-tested. Disclosure: 4 of my first planted rows were NOT red at HEAD (['cat','.env'] and the awk "cat " ".env" forms were already denied via the standalone `.env` literal, reason argv_path); I replaced them with `grep -r ssn data` forms, which are allowed at HEAD and denied with the change. One row stays ALLOWED on purpose: script-python-file-command-from-argv (a file that runs a command it is given).

TESTS. tests/exec_commands.rs: 11 real-binary tests (audit record read for the file named and the reason class): every bead form x 5 languages + awk, here-doc/here-string, wrappers (env, timeout, sh -c), -f / --file / -fFILE / shebang awk, refusal of built commands with the call named, deny/warn/allow stance, many-command cap, nested shells and scripts, nested 1..=7 levels, controls (print(1), awk '{print $1}', a regex's exec, asyncio.run, python -m x -c, heredoc as data to a script file). 25 unit tests in extract::exec.

GATES at 9101c0f. cargo fmt --check OK; clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0; full cargo test: 430 lib + 85 bin + every integration suite pass (operator_manifest caught my own "bd-5iy" in the README, fixed before the commit); tests/e2e_hook_matrix.sh against the built binary: 207/207 rows, p50 8.8 ms, max 26.9 ms. ubs: exec.rs and exec_commands.rs 0 critical; script.rs has 7 criticals on lines I did not add (enum `kind ==` read as a secret compare, Instant::now in an existing timing test): heuristic false positives.

MUTATION (hand-picked, scratch copy, 3 layers: matrix, real-binary, unit). 27 mutants of the wiring and exec.rs. 22 caught first time. 5 survived: 3 were test gaps (here-string program, awk -f file whose command names no path, `python3 -mX -c`): tests added, now caught. 2 were equivalent code I removed: `language != Awk` (interpreter_kind(awk) is None, dead) and `found.opaque = inner.is_opaque()` (command_extraction already marks empty argv opaque; is_opaque is argv.is_empty()). Writing the depth-guard mutant also found a real fail-open in my code: past MAX_DEPTH, inspect_inline returned silently, so a program nested 4+ levels deep (python -c running python -c ...) read as running nothing. Now it is reported opaque like a shell string nested too deep; test builds 1..=7 levels.

MEASURED FALSE-DENY COST. Replayed every interpreter command in local Claude Code transcripts (18,302 distinct python/node/bun/deno/perl/ruby/Rscript/awk commands) through the HEAD build and this one, scratch home, default config: 77 newly denied (0.65% of the 11,780 the old build allowed), 0 newly allowed. By cause: 38 a program or whole command built at run time, 24 the program run is a script veil reads and cannot analyse (typing that command is denied identically by the old build: ~/.airflow/af), 8 aws + 1 git given a computed word (the typed stance denies aws with an unresolved word too), 6 perl `exec @ARGV`. The FIRST replay had 138 newly denied, nearly all subprocess.run([..., var]) lists; that is why lists with a computed word are now judged as an unresolved word, not refused. Why files are not refused: of 922 real Python files under ~/Source/cmdrvl that mention subprocess/os, 721 (78.2%) would be denied if treated like a typed program (subprocess.run(cmd, ...)); typed programs are short, files are not. Numbers are in the README "False positives, measured".

KNOWN GAPS (README Script Files lists them; all measured ALLOWED on this build): a call renamed or looked up (s = os.system; s(cmd); getattr(os, "system"); from os import system as s), code in a string (exec/eval, base64), node `const {execSync: x} = ...`, perl `eval q{...}`, Ruby Kernel.send(:system, ...). A script file that builds its command is not refused. A script a same-line command writes first is bd-4uy (PeachFrog). A race between hook and run (file changes after veil reads it) is the existing TOCTOU limit. Over-block risk is the 0.65% above.

SEPARATE HOLE, filed as bd-u4u (P2, out of session scope; you may want P1): a command piped into a shell is the program it runs and is not read. All ALLOWED on HEAD and on this build: `echo 'cat .env' | sh`, `printf 'cat .env\n' | bash`, `echo 'cat .env' | bash -s`, `python3 -c "print('cat .env')" | sh`, `awk 'BEGIN{print "cat .env" | "sh"}'`. (`sh <<< 'cat .env'`, `sh <<'EOF'` and `sh -c 'cat .env'` are denied.) bd-5iy does not touch it.

d1a31fb, THE OPERATOR FLAKE. Cause: operator::tests::...combines_available_and_missing_tools writes a script (create_describe_tool: fs::write, chmod) and the operator execs it at once. On Linux an exec of a file any process holds open for writing fails with "Text file busy"; a sibling test thread that forks while the file is open keeps a copy of the write handle until its child execs, even though the writing thread closed it. Operator maps the failed spawn to status "error", so summary.available was 0, and the assertion printed only `0 != 1`. Reproduced on Linux (python:3.12-alpine, 8 threads starting processes): write-then-exec failed 2 times in 9,000 rounds (about 1 in 4,500, same rarity as the CI failure); deterministically with the fork window widened (22 busy retries, 0.46 s). macOS does not enforce ETXTBSY for exec (0 in my widened-window run), so it cannot fail there. Fix: create_describe_tool execs the script until it works (a successful exec means no one holds it open for writing, so every later exec works), retrying only on ExecutableFileBusy for up to 10 s, failing with the error itself otherwise; wait-first measured 0 failures in 9,000 rounds. The operator assertions now print the rendered report, so a tool that does not start says why. No assertion weakened. Verified: operator::tests:: x50 and the one test x50 on macOS (0 failures, but macOS cannot show the bug); full lib 430 pass with and without --features proptest; CI green on d1a31fb. NOT verified: I could not run the real Rust test on Linux (the Docker VM disk was full and I did not prune your images); the Linux evidence is the Python reproduction of the same kernel behaviour plus CI.

OTHER DISCLOSURES. The commit hook swept other agents' already-staged .beads/issues.jsonl lines into 9101c0f (bd-3rn, bd-jg9) and into d1a31fb; benign. Commit 3721122 (bd-3h5) says "121 blocked", actual 120. I started Docker Desktop (it was not running) for the Linux check and left it running.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED: everything above is my own execution at 9101c0f / d1a31fb; the mutation list, the replay and the file scan are mine and not re-run by anyone else.

title: Derived registration misses source edits when mtime is restored
description:
The source stamp in e3d9eff uses device, inode, length and mtime. A brokered authorized tool can rewrite a protected source in place, put its exact original bytes at a new `--out` path, then set the source mtime back. The checker reads the changed source after the tool returns and misses the copied bytes. The broker registers the copy, and the real Read hook allows it. This breaks the README claim that a file changing while the tool runs registers nothing.

Synthetic reproduction: `[sensitivity] protected = ["data/**"]`, `[spine] authorized_tools = ["profile"]`; fake `profile` does `before=source.stat(); original=source.read_bytes(); out.write_bytes(original); source.write_bytes(b"Z"*len(original)); os.utime(source, ns=(before.st_atime_ns,before.st_mtime_ns))`. It reports device/inode/size/mtime before and after.

At fixture cwd with isolated `HOME`, fake tool first on `PATH`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=s1`:

`/tmp/veil-review-e3d9eff-target-lUxIv1/debug/veil exec profile race data/memo.txt --out data/race-copy.txt`

Exit 0, stdout empty. Observed identical stamp on both sides: `16777223:719525920:450:1795668866629744480`. The source is now 450 `Z` bytes; the output contains the original 450 bytes. `veil derived verify data/race-copy.txt --json` returned exit 0 and `status=registered`, hash `blake3:7774bbb86b5c72a5c490aa871dd4d22afb4e2cb6c1175dadbaea2de8b6bc9492`. A real PreToolUse Read returned allow; the audit reason was `derived: output of `profile` registered by veil exec (this session)`.

Likely fix: include filesystem change time in the source stamp, or compare candidates against source content/digests captured before the tool starts. Add this as a real-binary regression that asserts the copied path remains denied.
close_reason: Verified (fix f4c8a97, CI 45762216389 green). Orchestrator re-execution from clean git-archive exports: a_source_rewritten_with_its_stamp_put_back_registers_nothing FAILS on 0814607 source and passes at 0b3ea61; full suite with proptest at 0b3ea61 886 passed 0 failed (macOS). Reviewer retested the real binary at dd00647: original repro, replace, rename, mmap rewrite, symlink retargets and a concurrent rewrite of an 8360-byte source all refused. Limits: a protected source CREATED during the run is not compared and can be registered (README: only files present when the tool starts); a 1.65 MiB race case timed out in the reviewer harness and is unverified.

comments.author: zacharyruiz
comments.text:
MagentaBass: pushed f4c8a97 (main and master). CI run 45762216389: success, 5/5 jobs (rust, linux-landlock-sandbox, macos-seatbelt-sandbox, e2e-hook-matrix ubuntu + macos, 212/212 rows on both). The new test is ok in the Linux rust job (both test steps) and in the macOS job step that proves the derived registry under Seatbelt. Left open for verification.

FIX: veil hashes every file it will compare BEFORE the tool starts. After the run a comparison counts only if the bytes searched have that hash, taken in the same read pass as the search. The stamp check stays. I did not add ctime: a stronger stamp still would not show which bytes were compared. All in src/derived.rs; broker.rs not changed.

RED: with only the stamp check (my new comparison removed, rest of the change in place), the real hook answered allow for the copy in all four cases of a_source_rewritten_with_its_stamp_put_back_registers_nothing: named protected file; named file only a pack classifies (.env); protected file reached through a list; standard output. The first red run, on unchanged e7176b6 source, stopped at case 1 with allow. The test asserts the tool restored dev, inode, length and mtime to the nanosecond.
MY FIRST DRAFT of the test was partly vacuous: the cases shared one project, so the copy left by one case made veil refuse the next for repeating it, and cases 2 and 3 would have been refused without the fix. The message assertion caught it; each case now has its own project and its text is in one file only.

YOUR REPRODUCTION, replayed from the bead text as a Python tool using os.utime (scratch probe, not committed), release builds. e7176b6: stamps identical, exec exit 0, derived verify exit 0 registered, Read hook allow. f4c8a97: stamps identical, veil says memo.txt changed while the tool ran, derived verify exit 1 not_registered, Read hook deny.

COST: every veil exec with something to compare now reads it twice, whatever the tool prints. Release builds, one Mac, median of 5 runs, e7176b6 -> fix: 1000 files / 195 MiB 3063 -> 3195 ms; 60 files / 960 MiB 14806 -> 15720 ms; 4 tiny files no measurable change. (The baseline is already that slow at these sizes.) A file veil cannot read now fails the first read; as before, nothing registers.

COMMANDS, on base 0814607 plus the change: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --features proptest -- -D warnings; same without the feature; same with --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (rustup toolchain bin first on PATH); PROPTEST_RNG_SEED=314159265 cargo test --locked --features proptest --no-fail-fast: 881 passed, 0 failed; cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast: 874 passed, 0 failed; ast-grep scan: 2 HashMap warnings on untouched lines; cargo build --locked, then tests/e2e_hook_matrix.sh --veil target/debug/veil --run-dir <scratch>: 212/212; ubs src/derived.rs tests/derived.rs: 2 critical (1 panic!, 1 non-crypto randomness), same as e7176b6. GraySpring committed 0814607 during my first full run, so I reran clippy, both suites, ast-grep and e2e with HEAD unchanged throughout. No existing test expectation changed. README: how the check works, its cost, and that only files present when the tool starts are compared.

NOT DONE / NOT VERIFIED: an mmap rewrite, and a coarse-timestamp filesystem, are not tested; the new check does not look at how a file was changed, which is why I expect it to hold, but that is reasoning. I did not test a process that keeps rewriting a source while veil is reading it. The limits already in README stay: a tool can still emit protected values in a shape the text comparison does not see (re-encoded, reordered), which needs no timestamp trick.

ALSO: after 0814607 the shared index held the bead file from before that commit (MM in git status), so a plain commit would have reverted three of GraySpring bead comments and dropped bd-szf. The working tree matched HEAD; I ran git add on that one file and told GraySpring. I saw bd-szf (reviewer, new, unassigned) and did not touch it.

comments.author: zacharyruiz
comments.text:
Independent review of the fix at clean archived revision `dd006477ea1faef4b7c4905f7f8139e628cbd264` (after f4c8a97). All sources, configs, outputs and fake tools were synthetic fixtures under `/tmp`; no repo source was edited.

Commands:
- `git archive dd00647 | tar -x -C /tmp/veil-review-dd00647-lilacox-cFOg2z`
- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/veil-review-dd00647-target-lilacox-GgPsjK cargo build --locked --bin veil` — PASS.
- `python3 -m py_compile /tmp/veil_dd00647_registration_probe.py` — PASS.
- `python3 /tmp/veil_dd00647_registration_probe.py` — replay and cases below completed; its 1.65 MiB concurrent case exceeded the harness's 120 second timeout, so that size is UNVERIFIED.
- `python3 /tmp/veil_dd00647_registration_probe.py --race-only` — completed with an 8,360-byte source.

**PASS: original bd-5ks repro is fixed.** In an isolated HOME with `data/**` protected and fake `profile` first on PATH, ran `veil exec profile restore data/memo.txt --out data/copy.txt`. The tool copied the synthetic original, overwrote the source in place with same-length `Z` bytes, then restored atime/mtime. Before/after device, inode, length and mtime were identical. Exit 0; stderr said `not registered ... memo.txt changed while the tool ran`; `veil derived verify data/copy.txt --json` exited 1 with `status=not_registered`; real PreToolUse Read returned `deny`.

**PASS: replacement/rename, mmap and symlink retargets fail closed.** The exact broker calls in the harness were `veil exec profile replace data/memo.txt --out data/copy.txt`, `veil exec profile rename data/memo.txt --out data/copy.txt`, `veil exec profile mmap data/memo.txt --out data/copy.txt`, `veil exec profile symlink-file data/source-link.txt --out data/copy.txt`, and `veil exec profile symlink-dir data/alias/source.txt --out data/copy.txt`. Each fake tool first copied the original synthetic bytes to `--out`; then it atomically replaced the source, renamed it away, rewrote it through mmap while restoring mtime, retargeted a file symlink, or retargeted a directory symlink. The symlink cases started with the source path denied by the protected policy. Each output was refused with `not registered` / `changed while the tool ran`, `derived verify` exited 1, and Read returned `deny`.

**PASS: concurrent rewrite test at smaller size.** `python3 /tmp/veil_dd00647_registration_probe.py --race-only` ran `veil exec profile race data/memo.txt --out data/copy.txt /tmp/v5k-l5mkgu3w/concurrent-rewrite/bin/writer.py /tmp/v5k-l5mkgu3w/concurrent-rewrite/writer.done`. The fake tool copied all 8,360 original bytes to the output and launched a fixture writer that toggled the source between those bytes and `Z` while restoring mtime each write. The broker call took 1.193 seconds; the writer ran 1.5 seconds and completed 3,577 writes. Source device/inode/length/mtime were equal before and after. Veil said `not registered ... memo.txt changed while the tool ran`; verify exited 1 and Read returned `deny`. This establishes overlap during the broker's source comparison and no escape in this probe.

**Expected documented limit, not a new bug: source created during the run.** `veil exec profile create data/new-source.txt --out data/copy.txt` started with the protected path absent. The fake tool created the protected source and copied it to `--out`; exit 0, verify returned `registered`, and Read returned `allow`. README Derived Outputs / “What stays possible” says only named/protected files present when the tool starts are compared. This behavior is within that stated limit, not a break of the before-tool hash guarantee for files captured at start.

Broken guarantee found: none in the tested routes. The large 1.65 MiB race attempt timed out after 120 seconds and is unverified; the completed 8,360-byte concurrent test is the race result above. I did not retest transformed/re-encoded output or a coarse-timestamp filesystem; README already identifies text comparison's transformed-value limitation.

title: Track A: audit log path-extraction noise and schema cleanup
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic. Depends on shell decomposition.

PROBLEM: ~/.cmdrvl/logs/veil/audit.jsonl contains entries whose 'path' is 'dir>' or '2>/dev/null' or '/Users/zac/Source/cmdrvl/verify/2>/dev/null': redirections are being resolved as paths. Also the file mixes schema generations and jq stops parsing partway (only 538 of 7624 lines parse with the current key set).

FIX: strip redirections in the decomposer; add 'schema_version' to entries; add 'veil audit --validate' that reports unparseable lines; document rotation (size-based, keep 5).

TESTS: decomposer strips 2>/dev/null, >out, <in, 2>&1 and never emits them as paths (regression fixtures from the real audit log); schema_version present on every new entry; 'veil audit --validate' reports the count of unparseable legacy lines on a fixture mixing generations; rotation keeps 5 files.
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator at 0175c50: full suite 650 passed, 0 failed on clean export; CI green. Audit log: whole lines, schema version, --validate, tolerant reads, rotation; redirect-glued-word fixes. Author corrected its timing note: the 1 ms decompose test has about 2x margin quiet and none under load (flake risk, sent back to %5 to harden). comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
bd-5zy evidence (BrownChapel). Bead left open for independent verification.

Commits on main: 833e27d (redirect fix, SECURITY), b086f3f (scan overhead trim), 0175c50 (audit log). CI rust job green on 833e27d and 0175c50. 659b513 (PeachFrog's, before mine) failed CI on the 4 KiB timing test, see gaps.

FOUND WHILE DOING THIS: a security bypass, not only log noise.
At 6ddaa25 the decomposer left `.env>out.txt` as one word, which no protected pattern matches. With only the built-in packs and no project config, a clean HEAD build ALLOWED `cat .env>out.txt`, `cat .env>>out.txt`, `cat .env&>/dev/null`, `cat .env>&2`, `head -1 .env>out.txt` (spaced `cat .env 2>/dev/null` was DENY). Same with a file-naming pattern: `cat data/holdings.csv>out.txt` ALLOWED under `**/holdings.csv`. The same missing separation is also what wrote `<cwd>/2>/dev/null` into the log as a path.
Fix (833e27d): scanner ends the word before an unquoted `<`, `>` or `&>` unless that word is a bare fd number (`2>x`, `10>x`) or the operator is still going (`>>`, `>&`, `>|`). `holdings.csv2>x` is the file `holdings.csv2` plus a redirect, as in the shell; quoted/escaped operators are data. cat, bat/less/more and head/tail collectors no longer take an attached redirection word as a file.

AUDIT LOG (0175c50), against the bead's list:
- schema_version "veil.audit.v1" on every new record. Test: every_new_record_says_which_schema_it_is.
- `veil audit --validate` (text and --json): lines, current, legacy, unparseable, blank, first 20 unparseable line numbers. Always exits 0 when the file is readable; conflicts with --class (exit 2). `veil audit` itself now skips non-entry lines and reports skipped_lines instead of aborting at the first bad one.
- Rotation: 10 MiB, keep 5 (oldest deleted, as the bead says), advisory lock on <log>.lock, size re-checked under the lock. A failed rotation still writes the record and reports on stderr.
- Root cause of "jq stops parsing partway" that the bead did not name: serde_json::to_writer on an unbuffered file wrote one syscall per token, so concurrent hooks interleaved bytes. Now one write_all of a prebuilt line. The 16-hooks-x-8-records test reads back whole.
- README "Audit Log" section and operator.json (--validate, usage line) updated. README previously implied a non-protected word writes no record; direct readers do record allowed files, now stated.

EVIDENCE:
- Clean copy = HEAD plus only my files: full `cargo test --locked` 650 passed 0 failed; clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --check clean; ubs 0 critical on the files I added (tests/audit_log.rs had one panic!, replaced).
- tests/redirections.rs (real binary): on 6ddaa25 it fails 3 of 4; on the fix it passes 4 of 4. Includes a parity test: 21 programs x 3 configs x 5 operators, glued form must get the same decision as the spaced form.
- Mutation checks, each fails at least one test: R1 no separation (7 tests), R2 `&>` not separated (5), R3 no fd rule (4), R4 reader keeps redirection words (1), A1 piecewise writes (3), A3 no schema_version (7), A4 abort on bad line (2), A5 keep 6 (1).
- A2 (remove the re-check under the lock) SURVIVED my first test set: the stress test used keep=500, where a duplicate rotation loses nothing. I added a test that holds the lock while a second hook waits, plus a "no rotated file under the limit" invariant on the stress test; A2 is now caught 3 of 3 runs. My original doc comment ("ten megabytes would be gone") was also wrong and is corrected: the cost is a near-empty file pushing the oldest real one out of the five.

GAPS AND CHOICES, stated plainly:
- No independent verification. Mutation checks are mine, run on a scratch copy.
- The lock test sleeps 300 ms so the second hook is waiting. If that hook is slow to start the test passes whatever the code does; it cannot fail on correct code, but it can miss the mutant on a loaded machine.
- Timing: `four_kib_of_command_decomposes_in_under_a_millisecond` (1 ms limit, best of 50, debug build) failed on CI at 659b513 with 1.03 ms and locally under load average 37. My scanner change added about 4-5% (about 0.53 to 0.55 ms for 4082 bytes at quiet load); b086f3f only tests the first character before the all-digits scan. The margin is still roughly 2x on a quiet machine and the test is unchanged. I did not weaken it.
- Not repaired: existing damaged lines in anyone's real log. --validate reports them; nothing rewrites or migrates them.
- Rotation size and file count are fixed constants, not config. `veil audit` reads only the current file, so entries just before a rotation are in .1.
- Test fixtures are synthetic, modelled on the shapes in the real log (redirect-as-path, eight- and ten-key legacy records, interleaved lines). I did not copy the real log into the repo: it holds this machine's paths and session ids.
- `2>/dev/null cat file` is judged under argv_path, not direct_read, a classification quirk I left alone.
- Only `<`, `>`, `&>` and their forms were examined. I did not look at process substitution `<(...)`/`>(...)`, here-doc bodies, or other redirection syntax beyond what tests/redirections.rs lists.
- macOS developer machine plus CI's rust job; nothing else tested. File::lock is the std advisory lock.
- Priority: the bypass may deserve its own bead and a higher priority than this P3. Asked in mail 15981, not answered yet.

comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
Correction to my bd-5zy evidence comment (timing bullet).

I wrote that the scanner change added "about 4-5% (about 0.53 to 0.55 ms for 4082 bytes at quiet load)". Those readings were taken at load average about 33, not at quiet load. What I measured, best of 50 runs, debug build, 4082 bytes:
- load about 33, 3 rounds: with the redirect fix 563 / 543 / 549 us, without it 528 / 527 / 526 us (3 to 6% slower).
- load about 4, 3 rounds: with the first-character test (b086f3f) 435 / 510 / 438 us, the redirect fix as first pushed (833e27d) 469 / 453 / 537 us. At that load the two overlap and I cannot claim a difference in either direction.
So: the overhead was a few percent under load and not measurable on a quiet machine; the margin to the 1 ms limit is about 2x when quiet and gone when the machine is loaded or CI is slow. The test is unchanged and is still a flake risk.

comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
bd-5zy follow-up (BrownChapel): the decompose timing test is now independent of load. Commit 31749a5, CI rust job green (run 45694566311). Not independently verified.

Replaced four_kib_of_command_decomposes_in_under_a_millisecond (best of 50 against 1 ms; failed on CI at 659b513 with 1.03 ms) with decomposing_a_command_is_cheap_and_grows_with_its_length. Two checks, all work measured in one process with the workloads taking turns inside each of 300 rounds, best of each:
- linear: cost per byte of a long command (16 KiB for the uncapped single segment, 3.8 KiB for the nested shape, the cap for the third) against a 0.5 KiB one of the same shape. Bound 1.5. Measured 0.74 to 0.91 idle, with 24 and 32 busy processes on 16 cores, and in release.
- cheap: the cost of decomposing in passes of a trivial byte loop over the same bytes. Bound 40 in debug, 46 in release. Measured 9 to 21 in debug (idle and busy), 12 to 23 in release.
The absolute times moved a lot (the 16 KiB case 1.3 ms idle, 2.4 ms busy) while both ratios stayed put.

Mutation checks on a scratch copy: a rescan of the segment text once per token (mildest quadratic I tried) shows 1.71 to 1.73 and fails 3 of 3; tripling the work fails 3 of 3 (48 passes on the capped shape, the other two shapes stay under 40); a deeper quadratic is not needed to be shown because the mild one already fails.

Limits, plainly: DOUBLING the work passes (25, 18, 33 passes), tripling fails; that is the same sensitivity the old 1 ms test had against a 0.45 ms quiet machine, no better. My first version had a 3.0 growth bound and a 4 KiB size, and the mild quadratic mutant SURVIVED it (it was invisible at 4 KiB, and the old test would not have seen it either); I tightened to 1.5 and added the 16 KiB shape because of that. The old test's "long segment" was really the past-the-cap shape; the new test says so. The bounds are calibrated on this one machine (macOS, 16 cores) and debug/release builds; a much slower or differently scheduled CI runner is not something I measured, only CI's run on Linux passed once.

title: Evaluate access decisions from normalized inputs
description:
## Scope
Build the evaluator that combines allowlist, sensitivity classification, protected-directory context, spine-tool authorization, and policy selection into one decision.

## Deliverables
- `src/evaluator.rs`
- deterministic evaluation order
- confidence propagation onto the final decision
- fail-open behavior for internal error or timeout paths, with audit-friendly metadata

## Out of Scope
- hook stdin parsing
- stdout or stderr rendering
- audit log persistence itself

## Acceptance Criteria
- integration tests cover allowlisted path, non-sensitive path, sensitive direct read, sensitive spine invocation, and directory-sensitive file outside a protected directory
- internal error or timeout paths fail open and preserve a reason suitable for audit logging
- evaluator output is a single `Decision` value that downstream hook mode can render directly
close_reason: Completed

title: Some commands take veil so long that the harness may give up on the hook
description:
Found while working on bd-chg. Some very long or deeply nested commands make the check take tens of seconds, with time that grows faster than the command does: 28 seconds was the longest measured in a release build, on an Intel Mac, and that one then crashed, which bd-chg now blocks. A harness that stops waiting for a hook can let the call through. No run past a harness timeout was observed, and veil install sets no timeout of its own.

Done when: the time to check a command is bounded, and a command veil cannot check within the bound is refused, with a test through the real binary.

title: Hook allows protected reads in shell strings it never reads (unlisted runner, leading redirect, trap action, code in a variable)
description:
Found while fixing bd-szf (7d5a017). Each command below gets
`permissionDecision=allow` from the hook and, except where noted, prints a
synthetic protected file under macOS /bin/bash 3.2. Project config:
`[sensitivity] protected = ["protected/**"]`. These are older gaps in what the
hook reads, not spine authority: no tool is involved.

1. A runner veil does not unwrap, so the shell string is never read:
   `caffeinate bash -c 'cat protected/x.csv'`
   `script -q /dev/null bash -c 'cat protected/x.csv'`
   `sandbox-exec -p '(version 1)(allow default)' bash -c 'cat protected/x.csv'`
   Also allowed, bytes not shown here: `arch -arm64 bash -c ...` (printed
   nothing on this machine), `stdbuf -oL bash -c ...` (not installed here).
   `script -q /dev/null cat protected/x.csv` IS denied: the path is a word.
2. A redirection written before the command is taken for the program:
   `>/dev/null bash -c 'cat protected/x.csv >&2'`
   `2>/dev/null bash -c 'cat protected/x.csv'`
   `< /dev/null bash -c 'cat protected/x.csv'`
   Allowed too: `A=1 >/dev/null bash -c '...'`.
3. Code in a variable's value that bash runs:
   `env 'BASH_FUNC_x%%=() { cat protected/x.csv; }' bash -c x`
   `PS4='$(cat protected/x.csv)' bash -xc true`
   `BASH_ENV='$(cat protected/x.csv >&2)' bash -c true`
4. A trap action is read only for changes to command lookup, not for reads
   (first noted in a bd-jn6 comment):
   `trap 'cat protected/x.csv' EXIT`

Related, not duplicates: bd-u4u (piped into a shell), bd-ob0 (a path inside
one quoted argument), bd-3pm (deferred backlog, unlisted readers).

Done when each case above is denied or is listed in README as a limit the
operator accepts, with a real-binary test that runs the command in bash for
every case the test machine can run. Item 2 touches redirect handling
(bd-bow); coordinate.
close_reason: Approved after independent review of 9017a1c; all blockers fixed, CI green, README limits accepted.
